docs.title: celldform
docs.text:
Start here

Project status: what exists, what has been measured and what has not. Installing on Windows: the desktop app, no Python needed.

Machine learning for measuring how SKBR3 breast-cancer cells deform in a dual-beam optical tweezer, and for classifying their HER2 expression (high or low) from that deformation.

Isaac Oppong-Baah — M.S. Electronics Engineering, Norfolk State University, 2026

Research software

Developed for an M.S. thesis and validated on 15 cells from one setup. It is not a medical device and must not be used for clinical decisions.

docs.title: What is celldform?
docs.text: celldform is a Python library, a set of command-line tools and a desktop app. It segments the trapped cell in each frame, measures its shape and deformation across a ramp of laser power, rejects frames that cannot be trusted, and classifies the cell's HER2 expression from how it deforms. The desktop app does that for a recorded video and shows the evidence behind the answer. The software is not real-time and is not connected to the instrument.

docs.title: Which way should I use it?
docs.text:
I want to... Use You need analyze a recording on Windows the Windows installer nothing else: Python and the libraries are inside analyze a recording with Python pip install "celldform[app]", then celldform-demo Python 3.10–3.12 use the library or repeat the research clone the repository, pip install -e ".[dev]" Python 3.10 or newer, a GPU helps

The trained models are not included. Before the app can analyze anything you load a segmentation model (the U-Net weights with their settings, or an nnU-Net checkpoint) and the HER2 classifier, or one model bundle: Required files.

docs.title: Pipeline at a glance
docs.text:
Stage What it does Module 1 — Acquisition Video → grayscale frames celldform.acquisition 2 — Preprocessing Denoise → CLAHE → morphology → resize → normalise celldform.preprocessing 3 — Segmentation U-Net: frame → cell mask celldform.segmentation 4 — Features Mask → shape and deformation measures, with frame checks celldform.features 5 — Classification Features → low / high HER2 celldform.classification, celldform.demo.framework 6 — Biomechanics Deformation rate and Kelvin–Voigt fitting celldform.biomechanics 7 — Desktop app Recording → HER2 class with evidence celldform.demo

See Pipeline Overview for the architecture.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/oppongbaah/cancer_cell_deformation.git
cd cancer_cell_deformation
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[app]"          # library + desktop app
pip install -e ".[dev]"          # test and lint tools
pip install -e ".[annotation]"   # napari, for mask annotation
pip install -e ".[docs]"         # MkDocs, for building these docs

On Windows without Python, use the installer instead.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Every script in scripts/ is also a console command named after it, so the whole pipeline runs from the shell without remembering paths:

celldform-train-experiment postswap/experiment_1b_loss e1b_lovasz_s42
# is exactly
python scripts/training/train_experiment.py postswap/experiment_1b_loss e1b_lovasz_s42
  • Naming: scripts/<stage>/<name>.py becomes celldform-<name> with _ turned into -. Each command runs its script with the current python and passes every argument through unchanged, so options, defaults, output and exit codes are the script's own. celldform-<command> --help is the authoritative option list; the per-command sections below show it as of 2026-10-07.
  • Umbrella: celldform on its own lists every command; celldform <command> [args] runs one (celldform train-experiment ... = celldform-train-experiment ...).
  • Install: pip install -e . (editable, from the repo). The scripts are not part of the installed package, so a non-editable install has the commands but they report that scripts/ is missing. celldform-annotate and celldform-annotate-frame also need pip install -e ".[annotation]" (napari).
  • Working directory: like python scripts/..., commands resolve relative paths (configs, data, results) against the current directory, so run them from the repo root.
  • On the NSU cluster: the training and evaluation commands have SLURM job scripts under scripts/hpc/ that take the same arguments, e.g. sbatch scripts/hpc/training/train_experiment.sh .... See HPC Guide.
  • No command: scripts/hpc/ (submit those with sbatch) and scripts/maintenance/ (one-off migrations; re-running them would move files again).

tests/test_cli.py keeps the commands, scripts/ and pyproject.toml in sync: a new script without a command, a command without a script, or a script without an argument parser fails the tests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Data

Command What it does celldform-demo Desktop app: HER2 class of a trapped cell from a recording (U-Net or nnU-Net) celldform-organize-dataset Build pipeline-ready frame folders from data/raw/ celldform-extract-frames Data acquisition — extract frames from an optical tweezer video recording. celldform-preprocess-frames Apply PreprocessingPipeline to annotated frames and save the outputs to disk. celldform-build-randswap Build one randswap fold: draw the cell split from the config, then preprocess its data. celldform-build-nnunet-dataset Build the nnU-Net benchmark dataset from the randswap cross-validation -- same frames, same folds. celldform-build-distill-data Distillation data for one randswap round: our round-k training data + nnU-Net (teacher) targets.

Annotation

Command What it does celldform-annotate Interactive cell annotation tool — napari-based. celldform-annotate-frame Annotate or correct specific frames in napari, one after the other. celldform-preview-masks Colorized masks — render saved masks as real color PNGs, viewable directly in any image viewer (no napari needed). celldform-validate-masks Validate the masks that are present in the annotation pool.

Training

Command What it does celldform-train-unet Train U-Net for cancer cell segmentation. celldform-train-experiment Train + evaluate one run of an experiment, keeping every artefact inside that experiment's folder (2026-09-30 layout: one folder per experiment, mirrored under configs/… celldform-train-cv-fold One randswap cross-validation round: draw + build the fold's data, train, score. celldform-train-deploy-model The randswap DEPLOYMENT model -- the one RealTimePipeline runs on the camera: every cell trains, fixed length = the CV median best epoch. celldform-train-nnunet-cv nnU-Net benchmark: the randswap cross-validation, round for round, with nnU-Net in place of our U-Net. celldform-train-student-cv Distillation student CV (Experiment 6): every randswap round, against our CV model at the same epoch. celldform-distill-ensemble Distil the 4-seed ensemble into a single deployable U-Net.

Evaluation

Command What it does celldform-evaluate-unet Evaluate a trained U-Net on the holdout set and report segmentation metrics. celldform-eval-native Score a checkpoint on the testing set at NATIVE resolution (1228x922). celldform-eval-testing-set Score one checkpoint on the testing set (the four held-out cells, on disk 02_unet_holdout / preprocessed postswap_devset): each cell, then all cells pooled. celldform-eval-nnunet Score one round of the nnU-Net benchmark exactly as eval_native.py scores our U-Net. celldform-ensemble-eval Evaluate an ensemble of checkpoints on the development set. celldform-eval-ensemble-cv Ensemble test (report: Pending 1, "the gate"): our U-Net + nnU-Net, averaged, on the randswap rounds. celldform-summarize-cv Summarise a randswap cross-validation: every round, every cell, one headline. celldform-compare-postswap Compare postswap runs against the series baseline, on the development set. celldform-check-convergence Flag training runs that converged poorly, before their numbers enter a mean. celldform-latency-benchmark Frame-to-mask latency: our U-Net against nnU-Net, measured the same way on the same frames.

Inference

Command What it does celldform-infer End-to-end inference on optical tweezers video data. celldform-predict-single-frame Quick sanity check — run a trained U-Net checkpoint on one raw frame and draw two outlines on top of it: a solid line around each predicted region (the actual, possibly… celldform-harvest-factory Segment every 03_mask_factory frame with the ensemble and extract classifier features.

Report figures and tables

Command What it does celldform-build-report-assets Regenerate every figure and table in the current progress report. celldform-make-report-tables Generate the progress report's LaTeX tables from the data. celldform-make-cell-gif Social-media GIF: one trapped cell across the laser-power ramp, raw beside the model's outline. celldform-diagnose-false-positives Show what a checkpoint's false-positive region actually is, on the raw frame. celldform-render-holdout-comparison Render the four-figure holdout comparison used in the thesis progress reports: a strip of N frames from one holdout cell, shown as (1) raw unannotated frames, (2) the mu… celldform-view-soft-target Look at a teacher target (.npy) from the distillation data: the frame, its label, and the teacher's per-class probabilities as heat maps. celldform-plot-cell-sizes Per-cell trapped-cell size, measured from the annotation masks. celldform-plot-cv Figure and tables for the randswap cross-validation (1 October report). celldform-plot-data-map Dataset Organization figure (randswap): where every cell and frame goes. celldform-plot-experiments Figures for the experiments chapter of the 1 October report. celldform-plot-model-comparison The four candidate segmenters side by side, on the same 15 cross-validated cells: one small panel per measure, every value labelled. celldform-plot-nnunet-epochs nnU-Net at 100 against 1000 epochs on the same randswap rounds (8 October report). celldform-plot-percell-metrics Grouped bar chart of per-cell holdout metrics, read straight out of results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl — one panel per evaluation scope (each development-set cell, p… celldform-plot-pool-flow Provenance diagram of the frame pools: which cells go where, what draws from what, and where the evaluation firewall sits. celldform-plot-resize-vs-crop Experiment 3 figure: the same frames as each input variant sees them. celldform-plot-split-change Before/after of the train/validation/test split as two stacked bars. celldform-plot-sweep-dsc Horizontal bar chart ranking every checkpoint in results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl by its evaluated DSC on the development set. celldform-plot-fe-dataset Dataset Organization figure for the feature-extraction reports (22 October report onward). celldform-plot-features Feature-extraction figures and tables (22 October report). celldform-plot-final-models "Final Models at a Glance" -- the closing page of the 8 October report (written 2026-10-21). celldform-plot-high1-exclusion Why high-1 is excluded from the features (22 October report, feature extraction). celldform-plot-high10 Why high-10 is over-predicted in leave-one-cell-out round 14 (8 October report, added 27 October). celldform-plot-classification-thesis Classification chapter figures: every model's AUC and F1, per-cell P(high), the best model's chance null and its summary card. celldform-plot-analysis-dataset Dataset page of the analysis reports: what each cell contributes, and the leave-one-cell-out split. celldform-plot-loocv Leave-one-cell-out against the 5-fold cross-validation, for the U-Net and nnU-Net (15 October report). celldform-plot-protocols Dataset Organization figure, general form (15 October report): one rule, three protocols. celldform-plot-region-selection How the extraction picks the trapped cell, and why it drops a frame -- drawn on the predicted masks (22 October report, feature extraction). celldform-diagnose-mask-growth Where do a model's extra pixels go? Compare several runs' saved predictions of ONE test cell.

Features and classification

Command What it does celldform-extract-features Classifier features from the feature frames -- segment, validate every segmentation, then extract. celldform-benchmark-cells Per-cell HER2 benchmark: seven classical classifiers on the per-cell features, leave-one-cell-out. celldform-frames-cnn Per-frame HER2 classifier (deep learning), judged per held-out cell. celldform-power-resolution How many cells would a conclusive experiment need, and how small a deformation can the system resolve? celldform-tune-cells Hyperparameter tuning of the classical classifiers by nested leave-one-cell-out cross-validation. celldform-sequence-net Sequence networks on the deformation curves: can HER2 be told from HOW a cell deforms over the laser ramp? celldform-feature-ranking Feature rankings x k x classifiers, best-of-grid and nested choice, with permutation tests: does choosing features with the labels help? celldform-combine-models Frame- and step-level logistic regression and the soft-voting ensembles (equal-weight mean of P(high)), with permutation tests. celldform-pca-models PCA in place of feature selection: does compressing the features beat the selected 4? celldform-save-final-framework Fit the framework's HER2 classifier (step LR + LR on PC1 of the selected 4) on all 15 cells and save it for the demo. celldform-deformation-regression Deformation regression: does the strain grow with the laser power, and differently for high and low HER2 cells? celldform-rate-of-deformation Rate of deformation (RoD) per cell: measured over the full ramp, in real time, and predicted early.

HPC

Command What it does celldform-hpc-submit Generate and submit the SLURM U-Net training job on the NSU cluster

docs.title: celldform-demo
docs.text:
celldform-demo [recording_folder]
Opens the desktop app. It needs three files loaded before it can analyze (the U-Net weights, their settings and the HER2 classifier, or one model bundle): see the demonstration app. Headless: python -m celldform.demo.run <recording> --out <dir> --bundle models.zip.

docs.title: celldform-shortcut
docs.text: Creates (or with --remove deletes) a desktop shortcut for the app: celldform-shortcut [--start-menu] [--remove].

docs.title: celldform-organize-dataset
docs.text:
Build pipeline-ready frame folders from data/raw/.

celldform-organize-dataset
celldform-organize-dataset --raw-dir data/raw --every-n 100
celldform-organize-dataset --domain-adapt-n 10
celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean
celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean --domain-adapt-n 20   # run 2026-08-19, see Training Results — Domain Gap
celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean --config configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml  # same run, N from acquisition.domain_adapt_n
Option Default Description --raw-dir data/raw Root of raw data --frames-dir data/frames Output root for frame folders --every-n 200 Sample every N-th frame per video --config – Optional celldform YAML config; its acquisition.domain_adapt_n supplies the --domain-adapt-n default --domain-adapt-n 5 (or acquisition.domain_adapt_n when --config is given) Frames per cell copied into 01_annotate_pool across all 11 domain_adapt cells (raised to 20 as of 2026-08-19; recorded as acquisition.domain_adapt_n: 20 in configs/default.yaml and configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml). An explicit flag always beats the config value. Legacy frames reserved in 02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout/ are always excluded from the pool, regardless of N. --no-clean off Skip wiping --frames-dir before running

Implemented in the package (celldform.acquisition.organiser); scripts/data/organize_dataset.py is a thin wrapper around it.

docs.title: celldform-extract-frames
docs.text:
Data acquisition — extract frames from an optical tweezer video recording.

Script: scripts/data/extract_frames.py

celldform-extract-frames --video data/videos/experiment_01.mp4
celldform-extract-frames --video experiment.mp4 --output-dir data/frames
celldform-extract-frames --video experiment.mp4 --every-n 5
celldform-extract-frames --video experiment.mp4 --target-fps 10.0
celldform-extract-frames --video experiment.mp4 --max-frames 200
All options (--help) 
usage: extract-frames [-h] --video VIDEO [--config CONFIG]
                      [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--every-n EVERY_N]
                      [--target-fps TARGET_FPS] [--max-frames MAX_FRAMES]
                      [--target-size W H] [--format {png,tiff}]
                      [--change-threshold CHANGE_THRESHOLD]
                      [--dark-percentile DARK_PERCENTILE]
                      [--channel-width CHANNEL_WIDTH]
                      [--min-circularity MIN_CIRCULARITY]

Extract frames from an optical tweezer video recording.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --video VIDEO         Path to the input video file (.mp4, .avi, …).
  --config CONFIG       Path to YAML config file (default:
                        configs/default.yaml).
  --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Directory to write extracted frames (overrides config
                        data.frames_dir).
  --every-n EVERY_N     Keep every N-th frame (overrides config
                        acquisition.every_n).
  --target-fps TARGET_FPS
                        Resample to this frame rate in Hz (mutually exclusive
                        with --every-n).
  --max-frames MAX_FRAMES
                        Stop after this many frames (overrides config
                        acquisition.max_frames).
  --target-size W H     Resize each frame to W H pixels (overrides config
                        preprocessing.target_size).
  --format {png,tiff}   Output image format (overrides config
                        acquisition.image_format).
  --change-threshold CHANGE_THRESHOLD
                        Minimum trapped-cell centroid displacement (pixels)
                        required to save a frame. A frame is skipped when the
                        trapped cell has not moved this far from its position
                        in the last saved frame. Overrides config
                        acquisition.change_threshold.
  --dark-percentile DARK_PERCENTILE
                        Bottom X% of channel pixel intensities treated as
                        candidate cells. Default: 20. Overrides config
                        acquisition.dark_percentile.
  --channel-width CHANNEL_WIDTH
                        Width of the vertical flow channel as a fraction of
                        image width, centred at the horizontal midpoint (e.g.
                        0.30 = ±15% from centre). Overrides config
                        acquisition.channel_width.
  --min-circularity MIN_CIRCULARITY
                        Minimum circularity (4π·area/perimeter², 0–1) for a
                        blob to be accepted as a cell. Default: 0.60.
                        Overrides config acquisition.min_circularity.

docs.title: celldform-preprocess-frames
docs.text:
Apply PreprocessingPipeline to annotated frames and save the outputs to disk.

Script: scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py

celldform-preprocess-frames --masks
celldform-preprocess-frames --masks --compare --n-compare 5
celldform-preprocess-frames --pool 02_unet_holdout --masks
celldform-preprocess-frames --masks --target-size 128 128
celldform-preprocess-frames --image-dir data/frames/01_annotate_pool \
 \
    --output-dir data/preprocessed/frames/01_annotate_pool \
 \
    --mask-dir   data/masks/01_annotate_pool
All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-preprocess-frames [-h] [--pool POOL]
                            [--stage {train,evaluate,inference}]
                            [--image-dir IMAGE_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR]
                            [--compare] [--n-compare N_COMPARE]
                            [--compare-dir COMPARE_DIR] [--masks]
                            [--mask-dir MASK_DIR]
                            [--mask-output-dir MASK_OUTPUT_DIR]
                            [--crop-size CROP_SIZE] [--crop-center X Y]
                            [--legacy-crop-center X Y] [--target-size H W]

Preprocess annotated frames and optionally save pipeline figures

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --pool POOL           Pool folder name under data/frames/
  --stage {train,evaluate,inference}
                        Pipeline stage (default: auto-detected from --pool)
  --image-dir IMAGE_DIR
                        Override source image directory
  --output-dir OUTPUT_DIR
                        Override output directory for preprocessed frames
  --compare             Save pipeline stage comparison figures
  --n-compare N_COMPARE
                        Number of images to generate comparison figures for
                        (default: 5)
  --compare-dir COMPARE_DIR
                        Directory for comparison figures
  --masks               Also resize and save binary masks alongside inputs
  --mask-dir MASK_DIR   Source mask directory (default: data/masks/<pool>)
  --mask-output-dir MASK_OUTPUT_DIR
                        Override destination for resized masks
  --crop-size CROP_SIZE
                        Cut a native-resolution SIZE x SIZE window instead of
                        resizing the whole frame (experiment 3). Needs --crop-
                        center.
  --crop-center X Y     Crop centre in full-frame pixels for real-cell frames
  --legacy-crop-center X Y
                        Crop centre for legacy 2021 frames (their trap sits
                        elsewhere); defaults to --crop-center
  --target-size H W     Output spatial size (default: 256 256). Both dims
                        should be divisible by 16 for U-Net's 4 downsampling
                        steps.

docs.title: celldform-annotate
docs.text:
Interactive cell annotation tool — napari-based.

Script: scripts/annotation/annotate.py

celldform-annotate
celldform-annotate --image-dir data/frames/01_annotate_pool \
 \
    --mask-dir  data/masks/01_annotate_pool
celldform-annotate --pool 02_unet_holdout   # annotate holdout set
celldform-annotate --multiclass             # 3-class experiment (same 40 images)

Needs the annotation extra (pip install -e ".[annotation]") — it opens a napari window.

Option Default Description --pool 01_annotate_pool Pool folder name under data/frames/ and data/masks/ --image-dir – Explicit image folder (instead of --pool) --mask-dir – Explicit mask folder (instead of --pool) --multiclass off Annotate 3 classes (0 background, 1 trapped cell, 2 other/decoy) into data/masks/<pool>_multiclass/

docs.title: celldform-annotate-frame
docs.text:
Annotate or correct specific frames in napari, one after the other.

    domain_high_cell8_000000 domain_low_cell3_000000 domain_low_cell4_000000
celldform-annotate-frame frame_0000.jpg --mask-out custom/path.png

Needs the annotation extra (pip install -e ".[annotation]") — it opens a napari window.

Option Default Description images required Image files: full paths, or bare names resolved against data/frames/<pool>/ --pool 01_annotate_pool Pool used to resolve bare names and default mask paths --multiclass off Edit 3-class masks, saved to data/masks/<pool>_multiclass/ --mask-out mirrors data/masks/<pool>[_multiclass]/ Explicit output mask path (single image only)

docs.title: celldform-train-unet
docs.text:
Train U-Net for cancer cell segmentation.

Script: scripts/training/train_unet.py · SLURM job: scripts/hpc/training/train_unet.sh

celldform-train-unet --config configs/default.yaml
All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-train-unet [-h] [--config CONFIG] [--seed SEED]
                     [--domain-oversample-weight DOMAIN_OVERSAMPLE_WEIGHT]
                     [--fold FOLD] [--results-dir RESULTS_DIR]
                     [--epochs EPOCHS] [--save-last] [--tag TAG]

Train U-Net segmentation model.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG       Path to YAML config file.
  --seed SEED           Random seed (overrides config value).

docs.title: celldform-distill-ensemble
docs.text:
Distil the 4-seed ensemble into a single deployable U-Net.

Script: scripts/training/distill_ensemble.py · SLURM job: scripts/hpc/training/distill_ensemble.sh

celldform-distill-ensemble                      # cache targets, then train
celldform-distill-ensemble --cache-only         # just build the targets
celldform-distill-ensemble --temperature 3 --lambda-hard 0.5
All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-distill-ensemble [-h] [--config CONFIG] [--teachers [TEACHERS ...]]
                           [--cache CACHE] [--rebuild-cache] [--cache-only]
                           [--temperature TEMPERATURE]
                           [--lambda-hard LAMBDA_HARD] [--epochs EPOCHS]
                           [--run-name RUN_NAME]

Distil the 4-seed ensemble into a single deployable U-Net.

Why: the ensemble scores 0.859 evaluated against 0.809 for the mean single model,
and no per-cell collapse survives it. But it is an inference-time construct --
no checkpoint, 4x GPU per frame, and RealTimePipeline takes one UNet. Distillation
trains one student on the ensemble's *soft* outputs, so the student learns the
smoothed decision boundary the ensemble produces rather than only the hard masks.

How it works
------------
1. The teachers' averaged softmax is PRECOMPUTED over the training pool and cached
   to disk. Four teachers plus a student do not fit in 8 GB together, and caching
   also avoids 4 extra forward passes per batch per epoch.
2. The student trains on
       L = lambda * CE(hard masks) + (1 - lambda) * T^2 * KL(student/T || teacher/T)
   Hard labels are kept because the training pool *is* annotated -- the ensemble is
   a second opinion here, not the only source of truth. T > 1 softens both
   distributions so the student sees the teacher's relative confidences, not just
   its argmax; the T^2 factor restores the gradient scale that softening removes.
3. The split is the teachers' split (split_seed 42), so the student's validation
   slice is one no teacher trained on either.

Usage
-----
python scripts/training/celldform-distill-ensemble                      # cache targets, then train
python scripts/training/celldform-distill-ensemble --cache-only         # just build the targets
python scripts/training/celldform-distill-ensemble --temperature 3 --lambda-hard 0.5

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG
  --teachers [TEACHERS ...]
  --cache CACHE
  --rebuild-cache
  --cache-only
  --temperature TEMPERATURE
  --lambda-hard LAMBDA_HARD
                        Weight on the hard-label CE term; 1-lambda goes to the
                        KL term
  --epochs EPOCHS
  --run-name RUN_NAME

docs.title: celldform-ensemble-eval
docs.text:
Evaluate an ensemble of checkpoints on the development set.

Script: scripts/evaluation/ensemble_eval.py · SLURM job: scripts/hpc/evaluation/ensemble_eval.sh

celldform-ensemble-eval                      # all postswap seeds
celldform-ensemble-eval --runs A B C
celldform-ensemble-eval --save-log           # append to the eval log
All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-ensemble-eval [-h] [--runs [RUNS ...]] [--inputs INPUTS]
                        [--labels LABELS] [--ckpt-root CKPT_ROOT] [--log LOG]
                        [--save-log] [--name NAME]

Evaluate an ensemble of checkpoints on the development set.

Scores :class:`celldform.segmentation.ensemble.EnsembleUNet` -- the same class
``RealTimePipeline`` and ``infer.py`` run -- so the number reported here is the
number the deployed model produces. The combination rule (average the per-class
**softmax probabilities**, then argmax once) lives in that class and nowhere else;
changing it there changes what this script measures, by construction.

Averaging probabilities rather than voting on argmaxed masks keeps each model's
confidence, so a model that is unsure about a pixel does not get the same say as
one that is certain.

The per-member columns re-run each member through its own ``UNet.predict``, which
costs a second set of forward passes per frame (~2x). That is deliberate: both the
ensemble row and the member rows then come from shipped inference code rather than
from a copy of it written for this script.

Why this exists: on the 2026-09-23 three-seed baseline, `high-1` scored 0.818 /
0.833 / 0.507 across seeds (sd 0.184) while `high-9` sat at 0.043. That spread
is a property of the training run, not of the cell — seed 44 is behind on three
of four cells and on internal validation. An ensemble averages that variance out
instead of reporting it.

Costs 3x inference. Only Stage 3 uses the GPU, so this is the cheap part of the
pipeline to triple.

Usage
-----
python scripts/evaluation/celldform-ensemble-eval                      # all postswap seeds
python scripts/evaluation/celldform-ensemble-eval --runs A B C
python scripts/evaluation/celldform-ensemble-eval --save-log           # append to the eval log

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --runs [RUNS ...]     Run names under
                        checkpoints/postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline.
                        Default: postswap_ftl_cw142_s42 postswap_ftl_cw142_s43
                        postswap_ftl_cw142_s44 postswap_ftl_cw142_s45
  --inputs INPUTS
  --labels LABELS
  --ckpt-root CKPT_ROOT
                        Experiment folder holding the runs (default: the seed
                        baseline)
  --log LOG             Eval log --save-log appends to
  --save-log            Append the ensemble's metrics to the postswap eval log
  --name NAME           Name recorded in the log

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-compare-postswap [-h] [--log LOG] [--runs [RUNS ...]]
                           [--baseline BASELINE] [--seeds [SEEDS ...]]

Compare postswap runs against the series baseline, on the development set.

Exists to enforce the rule in configs/postswap/README.md that a single-seed
delta smaller than the noise floor is not a result. Measured spread on this
pipeline is sd ~0.047 pooled (3 seeds, split pinned), so a difference between
two single runs has SE ~ sd*sqrt(2) ~ 0.066 and needs roughly 2x that to be
believable. Deltas under that threshold are printed as INCONCLUSIVE, however
tempting they look -- this project has twice recorded a sub-threshold delta as
a finding and had to retract it.

Usage

python scripts/evaluation/celldform-compare-postswap                       # every run in the log

Script: scripts/evaluation/check_convergence.py · SLURM job: scripts/hpc/evaluation/check_convergence.sh

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-check-convergence [-h] [--ckpt-root CKPT_ROOT] [--runs [RUNS ...]]
                            [--tolerance TOLERANCE]

Flag training runs that converged poorly, before their numbers enter a mean.

Internal validation carries **no signal for comparing recipes** — the 2026-09-10
controlled re-run separated two checkpoints by 0.001 internally while the
development set separated the same two by 0.066. But it does detect a run that
simply trained badly, and that is a different question.

The case this exists for: `postswap_ftl_cw142_s44` reached internal val 0.905
against its siblings' 0.933 and 0.940, and went on to score 0.507 on `high-1`
against their 0.818 and 0.833 — dragging the 3-seed mean down and roughly
tripling the evaluated error bar. The bad run announced itself on a number that was
already being printed; nothing was looking at it.

Usage
-----
python scripts/evaluation/celldform-check-convergence                       # all postswap seeds
python scripts/evaluation/celldform-check-convergence --runs A B C
python scripts/evaluation/celldform-check-convergence --tolerance 0.015

options:

  --ckpt-root CKPT_ROOT

                        baseline recipe)
  --tolerance TOLERANCE
                        Flag a run this far below the best sibling (default
                        0.02)

two outlines on top of it: a solid line around each predicted region (the
actual, possibly irregular, area the network segmented) and a dotted line
around the hand-drawn ground truth, when one exists for that frame.

is fitting the trapped cell before committing to a full holdout evaluation.

checkpoints both load correctly without manual flags.

docs.title: celldform-benchmark-cells
docs.text:
Per-cell HER2 benchmark: seven classical classifiers on the per-cell features, leave-one-cell-out.

Script: scripts/classification/benchmark_cells.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-benchmark-cells [-h] [--model MODEL] [--config CONFIG]
                          [--perms PERMS] [--out OUT] [--replot]
                          [--only ONLY [ONLY ...]] [--selection-only]
                          [--final]

Per-cell HER2 benchmark: seven classical classifiers on the per-cell features, leave-one-cell-out.

    python scripts/classification/benchmark_cells.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--perms 1000]

One row per usable cell (features_cells.csv, usable == True), label high = 1. Every model sees the same
14 folds; scaling and missing-value filling are fitted inside each fold. Hyperparameters are FIXED in
advance (no tuning: with 13 training cells an inner search would mostly fit noise).

Feature sets
    selected  chosen from the 29 by a label-free selection, once, before any classifier (main):
                1. agreement  the per-cell value from the predicted masks against the same from the hand masks,
                              on the hand-masked frames: Spearman rho across the cells >= 0.8 (where testable)
                2. split-half the per-cell value from the even laser steps against the same from the odd ones,
                              on the feature frames: Spearman rho >= 0.8
                3. groups     the candidates are grouped by the correlation matrix (average-linkage clustering on
                              1 - |Spearman rho| across the cells, cut at |rho| = 0.7, as AutoSpearman); from each
                              group only its highest-ranked passing feature is kept
              ranked by the weaker of the two rho; every group's best passing feature is kept (no cap). The HER2 labels are never
              used, so the selection cannot leak the held-out cell.  -> feature_selection.csv / .tex
    all       every per-cell shape and deformation feature, no selection                       (sensitivity)
Baselines
    size      baseline length along the beam only
    image     per-cell medians of the whole-frame image measures (illumination, unevenness, contrast,
              noise). These track the recording session, not the cell: a classifier that does well on
              them is reading the session. Its score is the bar the cell features must clear.

Scores: correct cells, balanced accuracy, AUC of the held-out P(high), and a permutation p-value
(labels shuffled across cells, the whole leave-one-cell-out rerun, balanced accuracy).

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/:  feature_selection.csv / .tex, benchmark_cells.csv, scores_cells.csv
(every held-out cell's P(high) per model), benchmark_cells.png, benchmark_cells.tex.

Final models: after the run, every classifier on each feature set (and the size baseline) is fitted once on ALL
usable cells and saved with its leave-one-cell-out score -- the models a new cell is classified with
(celldform.final_models). --final does only this, from the saved selection and scores.
    -> checkpoints/classification/<model>/classical/<set>__<classifier>.joblib, manifest.csv

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL         feature run in results/features/
  --config CONFIG       settings file (default
                        configs/analysis/classifiers.yaml)
  --perms PERMS         label shuffles for the permutation p (0 = skip;
                        default: the config's)
  --out OUT             output folder (default results/classification/<model>)
  --replot              redraw the figure and table from the saved CSVs only
  --only ONLY [ONLY ...]
                        run only these classifiers (config names) and merge
                        them into the saved results
  --selection-only      only run the feature selection and write
                        feature_selection.csv (no classifiers)
  --final               only fit the final models on all cells and save them
                        (uses the saved selection and scores)

docs.title: celldform-frames-cnn
docs.text:
Per-frame HER2 classifier (deep learning), judged per held-out cell.

Script: scripts/classification/frames_cnn.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-frames-cnn [-h] [--model MODEL] [--config CONFIG] [--epochs EPOCHS]
                     [--device DEVICE] [--seed SEED]
                     [--variants {masked,mask} [{masked,mask} ...]]
                     [--seeds SEEDS [SEEDS ...]]
                     {crops,frozen,finetune,tune,final,report,all}

Per-frame HER2 classifier (deep learning), judged per held-out cell.

    python scripts/classification/frames_cnn.py crops      --model nnunet1000_loocv   # cut the cell crops once
    python scripts/classification/frames_cnn.py frozen     --model nnunet1000_loocv   # ResNet-18 features + LR
    python scripts/classification/frames_cnn.py finetune   --model nnunet1000_loocv   # fine-tune the last block
    python scripts/classification/frames_cnn.py report     --model nnunet1000_loocv   # table + figure
    python scripts/classification/frames_cnn.py final      --model nnunet1000_loocv --seeds 0 1 2
                                     # train on ALL cells, save to checkpoints/classification/<model>/cnn/

Data: every passing feature frame of the usable cells (~3 800 frames, ~6 per laser step).

Input -- built so the network cannot read the recording session from the frame:
    masked   a CROP x CROP px window centred on the trapped cell (the region the extraction kept), every pixel
             outside the (slightly grown) mask set to zero, intensity standardised over the cell's own pixels.
             The scale is NOT normalised: the cell's size stays in the input, as in the per-cell features.
    mask     the binary mask alone, same window (shape and size only; the control).

Models (ImageNet ResNet-18, grey crop copied to 3 channels):
    frozen    the pretrained network as a fixed feature extractor (512 numbers per frame) + logistic regression.
    finetune  the last residual block and a new head trained per fold (flips, 90-degree turns, mild intensity
              change), the laser step joined to the image features before the head. Cells are weighted equally
              (each cell's frames share one unit of weight), a fixed number of epochs (no peeking at the held-out
              cell).

Test: leave-one-cell-out, the same 14 folds as benchmark_cells.py. A held-out cell's frame probabilities are
averaged into one P(high) for the cell -- what a live system watching the cell would do.

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/:  cnn_frames_<variant>.csv (every frame's held-out P(high)),
cnn_cells.csv, cnn_cells.tex, cnn_frames_seen.png (accuracy against the number of laser steps watched).

positional arguments:
  {crops,frozen,finetune,tune,final,report,all}
                        tune: nested-CV hyperparameter tuning of the fine-
                        tuned cell-crop CNN; final: train on all cells and
                        save to checkpoints/classification/<model>/cnn/
                        (neither is part of all)

  --model MODEL
  --config CONFIG       settings file (default configs/analysis/cnn.yaml)

  --device DEVICE
  --seed SEED           fine-tuning seed (default: the config's)
  --variants {masked,mask} [{masked,mask} ...]
  --seeds SEEDS [SEEDS ...]
                        final step: one saved model per seed (default: the
                        config's seed)

docs.title: celldform-power-resolution
docs.text:
How many cells would a conclusive experiment need, and how small a deformation can the system resolve?

Script: scripts/classification/power_resolution.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-power-resolution [-h] [--model MODEL] [--tables TABLES]

How many cells would a conclusive experiment need, and how small a deformation can the system resolve?

    python scripts/classification/power_resolution.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--tables <report tables dir>]

Cells needed (from the usable cells of features_cells.csv and the selected features of benchmark_cells.py)
    per feature   Cohen's d between the classes (pooled SD), and the cells per class a two-sided Mann--Whitney
                  test needs to find a difference that size at alpha 0.05 with 80 % power:
                      n = 2 (z_0.975 + z_0.8)^2 / d^2 / 0.955     (0.955: its efficiency against the t-test)
                  d from 14 cells is itself uncertain (its 95 % interval is roughly +/-1.1), so n is an order
                  of magnitude, not a design figure.
    classifier    the cells (balanced classes) a one-sided binomial test needs to show that a classifier of a
                  given true accuracy beats 50 % at alpha 0.05 with 80 % power.

Resolution (from the passing feature frames: length along the beam, L_par)
    frame noise   median over cells and steps of SD/mean of L_par within a laser step (~6 frames)
    step noise    (a) frame noise / sqrt(frames per step) x 1.25 (the median's efficiency)
                  (b) from the step-to-step differences of each cell's step medians: SD(diff)/sqrt(2) -- an
                      upper bound, it also contains the cell's real step-to-step change
    detectable    a change between two steps: 2.77 x step noise (95 %); the strain over the ramp (last ten steps
                  against the baseline ten): 1.96 x sqrt(2/10) x step noise x 1.25; a compliance: 1.96 x the
                  standard error of the slope over 50 steps (x 1.1, the Theil--Sen efficiency)
    compared with the observed per-cell compliances and the difference between the class means.
    Random noise only: a segmentation error that grows with the laser power (high-1) is not in it.

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/: power.csv, resolution.csv, classify_power.tex, classify_resolution.tex.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL    feature run in results/features/
  --tables TABLES  also write the LaTeX tables here

docs.title: celldform-tune-cells
docs.text:
Hyperparameter tuning of the classical classifiers by nested leave-one-cell-out cross-validation.

Script: scripts/classification/tune_cells.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-tune-cells [-h] [--model MODEL] [--config CONFIG] [--perms PERMS]

Hyperparameter tuning of the classical classifiers by nested leave-one-cell-out cross-validation.

    python scripts/classification/tune_cells.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--config <yaml>] [--perms N]

Outer loop: each of the 14 cells is the test cell once. Inner loop, on the other 13 cells only: every point of the
classifier's grid (configs/analysis/classifiers.yaml, `tuning.grids`) is scored by leave-one-cell-out over the 13,
by the Brier score of their held-out P(high) (smoother than counting 13 calls; ties go to the earlier grid point).
The best point is refitted on the 13 and the test cell is scored once. The test cell never influences the choice,
so the outer scores are an honest estimate of a TUNED classifier -- comparable with the untuned benchmark
(benchmark_cells.py) on the same folds and the same selected features.

Permutation p: the cell labels shuffled and the WHOLE nested procedure rerun (`tuning.permutations`; the slow
tree ensembles are skipped). Outputs in results/classification/<model>/: tuning_cells.csv (per classifier),
tuning_choices.csv (the grid point chosen in every outer fold), tuning_scores.csv (held-out P(high)),
config_tuning.yaml.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL    feature run in results/features/
  --config CONFIG  settings (default configs/analysis/classifiers.yaml)
  --perms PERMS    label shuffles (default: the config's tuning.permutations)

docs.title: celldform-sequence-net
docs.text:
Sequence networks on the deformation curves: can HER2 be told from HOW a cell deforms over the laser ramp?

Script: scripts/classification/sequence_net.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-sequence-net [-h] [--model MODEL] [--config CONFIG] [--perms PERMS]

Sequence networks on the deformation curves: can HER2 be told from HOW a cell deforms over the laser ramp?

    python scripts/classification/sequence_net.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--config <yaml>] [--perms N]

Input, one per cell: the strain (%) of each measure (configs/analysis/sequence.yaml: length along and across the
beam, volume) at every laser step -- the median of the step's passing frames against the cell's own baseline
(celldform.biomechanics.rod.step_strain) -- a (measures x steps) curve. Missing steps are interpolated; a cell
with fewer steps is padded with its last value.

Models (deep learning, tiny on purpose: 13 training curves per fold):
    cnn1d  two 1-D convolution layers over the steps, global average pooling, a linear output
    gru    one recurrent (GRU) layer, its last state, a linear output

Training: leave-one-cell-out, the same 14 folds as every other model; each channel scaled by its SD over the
training cells; class-balanced loss; a random window of `crop` steps, noise and amplitude scaling per epoch; a
fixed number of epochs (no validation set). The held-out cell is scored on its whole curve; P(high) is averaged
over the seeds. Permutation p: labels shuffled and the whole leave-one-cell-out rerun (first seed only).

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/: seq_cells.csv (every cell's P(high), per model and seed),
seq_metrics.csv, config_sequence.yaml.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL    feature run in results/features/
  --config CONFIG  settings (default configs/analysis/sequence.yaml)
  --perms PERMS    label shuffles (default: the config's)

docs.title: celldform-feature-ranking
docs.text:
Feature rankings x k x classifiers, best-of-grid and nested choice, with permutation tests: does choosing features with the labels help?

Script: scripts/classification/feature_ranking.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-feature-ranking [-h] [--model MODEL] [--perms PERMS]
                          [--nested-perms NESTED_PERMS]

Which features, chosen how? Six feature rankings x seven feature counts x the eight classifiers, leave-one-cell-out.

    python scripts/classification/feature_ranking.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--perms N] [--nested-perms N]

The label-free selection (benchmark_cells.py) fixes 7 features before any classifier. This asks whether other
choices -- rankings that DO use the labels, and other feature counts -- do better. A ranking that uses the labels is
refitted inside every fold on the training cells only, so the held-out cell never influences which features it gets.

Candidates: the 29 per-cell features (15 shape medians + 14 deformation summaries; benchmark_cells.SHAPE + DEFORMATION).
Missing values are filled with the training cells' median and the features standardised before ranking.

Rankings (each orders the 29 features; the top k are used)
    label-free   the fixed label-free selection's order (feature_selection.csv), then the rest by its score -- the
                 same in every fold
    univariate   |AUC - 0.5| of each feature alone on the training cells (Mann-Whitney)
    mRMR         minimum redundancy, maximum relevance: greedily the feature with the highest univariate relevance
                 minus its mean |Spearman rho| with the features already chosen
    L1 path      L1 logistic regression on a falling penalty: the order in which coefficients become non-zero
    forest       random-forest impurity importance (300 trees)
    RFE          recursive feature elimination with logistic regression: drop the smallest |coefficient|, refit
Feature counts k: 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 29 (29 = every feature; the same for every ranking).
Classifiers: the eight of configs/analysis/classifiers.yaml, settings fixed (benchmark_cells.models()).

Three readings, from least to most honest
    grid         every (ranking, k, classifier): its leave-one-cell-out score. Exploratory: the best of 42 settings
                 per classifier is optimistic by construction.
    best of grid p   the permutation null of the BEST of the 42 settings (labels shuffled across cells, every ranking
                 and every fit rerun, the maximum AUC / balanced accuracy over the grid kept): the chance of a grid
                 maximum this high. Fast classifiers only (the linear models, RBF SVM, k-NN).
    nested       the ranking and k chosen INSIDE each fold, by leave-one-out over its training cells (lowest Brier
                 score), then the test cell scored once: an honest estimate of "pick the best features" as a method.
                 Logistic regression and k-NN, with a permutation p of the whole nested procedure.

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/: rank_grid.csv (every setting), rank_cells.csv (held-out P(high) of every
setting and the nested runs), rank_freq.csv (how often each feature is in the top 5, per ranking), rank_nested.csv,
rank_null.npz. The thesis figures are drawn by scripts/report/plot_classification_thesis.py.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL
  --perms PERMS         shuffles for the best-of-grid null (0 = skip)
  --nested-perms NESTED_PERMS
                        shuffles of the nested procedure (0 = skip)

docs.title: celldform-combine-models
docs.text:
Frame- and step-level logistic regression and the soft-voting ensembles (equal-weight mean of P(high)), with permutation tests.

Script: scripts/classification/combine_models.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-combine-models [-h] [--model MODEL] [--perms PERMS]

Frame- and step-level logistic regression, and combinations of the deep and classical models, leave-one-cell-out.

    python scripts/classification/combine_models.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--perms N]

Run after benchmark_cells.py, frames_cnn.py finetune (3 seeds), sequence_net.py and feature_ranking.py: it reads their
held-out P(high) per cell and fits nothing of theirs again.

Instance-level logistic regression (fitted here)
    every frame   one row per passing feature frame, the 15 shape measures + 5 per-frame deformation measures
                  (L_par, L_perp, volume, elongation f2, roughness); a held-out cell's P(high) = mean over its frames
    every step    the same, one row per laser step (median of the step's passing frames)
    Settings as the benchmark's logistic regression; scaling inside the fold; cells weighted by their rows. Permutation
    p: labels shuffled across CELLS (every frame of a cell keeps its cell's label), the whole thing rerun.

Combinations: the equal-weight mean of the members' held-out P(high) -- no weights are fitted, so nothing is learnt
from the test cell and a combination needs no extra validation. Called high at >= 0.5. Members: the CNN (fine-tuned,
cell crop, mean of 3 seeds), the eight classifiers on the label-free selection, LR and the ANN on all 29, the nested feature-ranking runs, the instance
LRs. A combination of classical models only has a permutation p (every member rerun under the same shuffle); one with
the CNN has none (one shuffle = 45 CNN trainings) -- it has a 2 000-resample cell-bootstrap interval on the AUC.

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/: instance_cells.csv, combine_cells.csv (every model's and combination's
held-out P(high)), combine_metrics.csv, combine_null.csv. The thesis figures are drawn by
scripts/report/plot_classification_thesis.py.

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL
  --perms PERMS

docs.title: celldform-pca-models
docs.text:
PCA in place of feature selection: does compressing the features beat the selected 4?

Script: scripts/classification/pca_models.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-pca-models [-h] [--model MODEL] [--perms PERMS]

PCA in place of feature selection: does compressing the features beat the selected 4? Leave-one-cell-out.

    python scripts/classification/pca_models.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--perms N]

Run after benchmark_cells.py and combine_models.py (it reads feature_selection.csv and the step-level LR's held-out
P(high) from instance_cells.csv).

What is fitted
    Three starting sets -- all 29, the 9 that pass reliability (rules 1-2), the selected 4 -- each standardised and
    reduced to its first k principal components (k = 1..6, below the set size), then a logistic regression (the
    benchmark's settings). PCA, imputation and scaling are fitted on the 14 training cells of each fold only, so the
    held-out cell never shapes the components. Each setting is scored alone and as the best model's ensemble
    (equal-weight mean with the step-level LR). The raw sets (no PCA) are in the grid as k = 0.

Statistics
    p            permutation of the whole procedure (labels shuffled across cells, step LR and every setting rerun)
    p_counted    the same shuffles, scored against the BEST balanced accuracy of the whole grid in each shuffle --
                 the p of "pick the best of the 36 settings", the choice actually made after seeing the results
    parallel analysis: the eigenvalues against those of 15 x n_features standard-normal data (5 000 draws); a
                 component is real only above the noise 95th percentile
    C sweep      the finalist and the current best model with both LRs at C = 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10

Outputs in results/classification/<model>/: pca_metrics.csv (every setting, per-class metrics, AUC interval, p,
p_counted), pca_cells.csv (held-out P(high)), pca_null.csv (every shuffle's score), pca_variance.csv, pca_loadings.csv, pca_csweep.csv.
The figure is cls_pca.png in scripts/report/plot_classification_thesis.py.

docs.title: celldform-deformation-regression
docs.text:
Deformation regression: does the strain grow with the laser power, and differently for high and low HER2 cells?

Script: scripts/biomechanics/deformation_regression.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-deformation-regression [-h] [--model MODEL] [--img IMG]
                                        [--tables TABLES] [--config CONFIG]

Deformation regression: does the strain grow with the laser power, and differently for high and low HER2 cells?

    python scripts/biomechanics/deformation_regression.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--img <dir>] [--tables <dir>]

One value per cell and laser step: the median of the step's passing feature frames (usable cells only), as a strain
in % against the cell's own baseline (median over steps 0-9), for three measures -- length along the beam, length
across it, and the spheroid volume. Each is fitted with a linear mixed-effects model:

    strain = b0 + b1 step + b2 high + b3 step x high  +  (u0 + u1 step | cell)  +  e

    b1   the typical low cell's strain per step (its compliance)
    b3   how much more (or less) a high cell strains per step -- the HER2 effect on deformation
    u1   each cell's own slope: the random slope makes the CELL the unit, not the ~700 step values

Fitted by REML (statsmodels MixedLM). A second fit adds the cell's baseline length (standardised) and its
interaction with the step, to ask whether size accounts for any HER2 effect.

How well it fits -- R^2 for mixed models (Nakagawa & Schielzeth 2013; random slopes as in Johnson 2014):
    marginal     variance of the fixed-effect prediction (step, HER2) / total variance
    conditional  (fixed + random-effect variance) / total variance -- the share explained once every cell has
                 its own line

Does HER2 help predict a new cell? -- leave-one-cell-out: each cell in turn is left out, both models are fitted
on the other 13, and the left-out cell's whole strain curve is predicted from the fixed effects alone (a new cell
has no fitted line of its own):
    with HER2     strain ~ step * high
    without HER2  strain ~ step
    zero          strain = 0 at every step (no deformation)
scored by the RMSE (percentage points of strain) over the cell's steps; the paired comparison is a Wilcoxon
signed-rank test over the 14 cells. HER2 and the recording session are the
same split in this dataset, so b3 cannot be told apart from a session effect.

Outputs in results/biomechanics/<model>/: deformation_regression.csv / .tex / .png (coefficients, fitted lines),
deformation_fit.csv / .tex (R^2 and leave-one-cell-out errors), deformation_loco.csv / .png (every cell's errors).

docs.title: celldform-rate-of-deformation
docs.text:
Rate of deformation (RoD) per cell: measured over the full ramp, in real time, and predicted early.

Script: scripts/biomechanics/rate_of_deformation.py

All options (--help) 
usage: celldform-rate-of-deformation [-h] [--model MODEL] [--img IMG]
                                     [--tables TABLES] [--config CONFIG]

Rate of deformation (RoD) per cell: measured over the full ramp, in real time, and predicted early.

    python scripts/biomechanics/rate_of_deformation.py --model nnunet1000_loocv [--img <dir>] [--tables <dir>]

RoD = slope of the strain (%) of the cell's length against the laser step (celldform.biomechanics.rod), for the
length along the beam (main) and across it, with a Newey-West 95 % interval. Usable cells, passing frames only.

    per cell     the full-ramp RoD of every cell, with its interval
    real time    the RoD from the first k steps only, k = 5, 10, ..., 50: how wide is the interval after k steps,
                 and how far is the estimate from the full-ramp RoD?
    early        leave-one-cell-out: the left-out cell's RoD after k steps, estimated four ways, against its full-ramp
                 RoD (the target):
                   own           its own k steps only
                   shrunk        own, combined with the prior from the other 13 cells (pooled)
                   shrunk+class  the same with a class-specific prior (the cell's HER2 class -- what a classifier
                                 would supply; the true class, so an upper bound on what classifying adds)
                   prior only    the other cells' mean RoD, no own data

Outputs in results/biomechanics/<model>/: rod_cells.csv, rod_realtime.csv, rod_early.csv, rod_cells.tex,
rod_realtime.tex, rod_cells.png, rod_realtime.png.

Final model: the settings and the priors from ALL usable cells (pooled, and per HER2 class), for estimating a new
cell's RoD (celldform.biomechanics.rod.estimate) -> checkpoints/biomechanics/<model>/rod_model.json

docs.title: Data Layout
docs.text:
Full documentation of the data/ directory. The data itself is not in the repository (see Data, models and logs); this page describes its layout so that the code and the scripts can be followed.

Snapshot of 2026-09-04

The folder structure and the contamination-firewall principle below still hold. The pool counts and which cells play which role changed afterwards: the final experiments split whole cells at random (5-fold and leave-one-cell-out, see Project status), and the machine that holds the data is the reference, not this page.

docs.title: Directory structure
docs.text:
data/
├── raw/                                Source recordings — never modified
│   ├── high/                           High HER2-expression cells (9 videos)
│   ├── low/                            Low HER2-expression cells (5 videos)
│   ├── cell 1 low 50 increments.mp4
│   └── legacy/20210825_cancer/         220 unlabelled JPGs from 2021 microscope
│
├── frames/                             Raw extracted frames (1228×922 greyscale JPEG)
│   ├── 01_annotate_pool/               U-Net training source (445 images: 200 legacy + 245 domain-adapt)
│   ├── 02_unet_holdout/                Development set — high_cell9 (50) + low_cell6 (51)
│   │   ├── legacy_holdout/             20 reserved legacy frames — separate diagnostic DSC
│   │   └── final_test/                 Blind test — high_cell10 (50), reserved, unannotated
│   └── 03_mask_factory/                Inference → classifier training (608 images)
│
├── masks/                              Hand-drawn masks (1228×922 PNG)
│   ├── 01_annotate_pool_multiclass/    U-Net training labels (0=bg, 1=trapped cell, 2=decoy)
│   └── 02_unet_holdout_multiclass/     Development-set ground truth (cell9 + cell6 done; cell10 pending, deliberately)
│
└── preprocessed/                       256×256 pipeline-ready data
    ├── train/01_annotate_pool_multiclass_256/
    │   ├── inputs/                     Preprocessed frames → U-Net training inputs
    │   └── labels/                     Resized masks       → U-Net training labels
    ├── evaluate/02_unet_holdout/
    │   ├── inputs/ · labels/           Development-set inputs/labels (cell9 + cell6 only)
    │   └── legacy_holdout/             Legacy-domain diagnostic inputs/labels
    ├── inference/03_mask_factory/inputs/  Preprocessed frames → classifier training
    └── comparisons/                    Pipeline stage figures (reporting)

There is no 04_clf_arena anymore — it was collapsed into 03_mask_factory on 2026-09-03 (its two cells, high_cell10 and low_cell5, became new U-Net training identities instead of a separate classifier-only firewall) and high_cell10 was then reassigned again on 2026-09-04 (see Cell roles below). If you're looking at an older doc, script comment, or memory that still mentions it, treat it as historical.

docs.title: Pool summary
docs.text: Pool Images Role Masks 01_annotate_pool 445 U-Net training source Hand-drawn, multiclass — 445/445 complete as of 2026-09-10 (low_cell5 was the last cell) 02_unet_holdout 101 Development set — U-Net + classifier, evaluated repeatedly to guide tuning Hand-drawn, multiclass (done) 02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout/ 20 Legacy-domain diagnostic — isolates domain gap from segmentation quality Hand-drawn, multiclass 02_unet_holdout/final_test/ 50 Blind test — high_cell10, reserved, one-shot None yet — deliberately deferred 03_mask_factory 608 U-Net inference → classifier training features (12 cells) U-Net-predicted (not hand-drawn)

docs.title: Three-tier evaluation terminology
docs.text:
Three genuinely different things get called "validation" or "test" informally — worth being precise, since an evaluated score from the wrong tier is easy to over-trust:

Tier What it is Where Used for Internal validation split Frames of cell identities the model has trained on (just held-out frames of them) data.val_split inside 01_annotate_pool, drawn fresh each training run Checkpoint selection and early stopping within one run. Not evaluated against real generalization — see the finding below. Development set Genuinely novel cells, never trained on, evaluated repeatedly across many recipes 02_unet_holdout (high_cell9 + low_cell6) Guides which hyperparameters/augmentations to keep. Not a blind test — every score here has shaped a decision. Blind test A reserved cell, evaluated exactly once, uninvolved in any decision 02_unet_holdout/final_test/ (high_cell10) The one honest, thesis-reportable generalization number — see Cell roles for the protocol that keeps it clean.

A smoke test (does the code run at all — shapes, dtypes, no crash) is a different concept entirely from any of the three above; it says nothing about model quality, only about basic correctness, and is cheap enough to run constantly.

docs.title: Cell roles
docs.text:
Role High cells Low cells U-Net training (01_annotate_pool, domain-adapt) 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 Development set (02_unet_holdout, top level) 9 6 Blind test (02_unet_holdout/final_test/) 10 —

Changed 2026-09-04. high_cell10 and low_cell5 were both folded out of the retired 04_clf_arena into training on 2026-09-03 — but by 2026-09-04, annotated training cells were imbalanced (7 high vs. 4 low), and per-cell evaluation had revealed high_cell9 and low_cell6 needed genuinely different treatment (see below). So low_cell5 stayed a training identity (grows the scarcer low-HER2 category), while high_cell10 moved to the holdout instead — as the reserved blind test, not a third development cell, since high_cell9/low_cell6 were already "spent" as a development signal.

high_cell10's frames are extracted the same way as high_cell9/low_cell6 (_extract_group(), every_n=200 across the full video — 50 frames, matching cell9's count exactly), but physically nested under 02_unet_holdout/final_test/ rather than sitting at the top level. This isn't just organizational: annotate.py, validate_masks.py, preprocess_frames.py, and evaluate_unet.py are all non-recursive (iterdir()/glob-based), so a routine --pool 02_unet_holdout command physically cannot see into final_test/ — mirroring the existing legacy_holdout/ pattern. Combined with high_cell10 having no masks yet at all (so it can't be scored even if pointed at directly), this is a hard, structural guarantee against the blind test leaking into development, not just a convention to remember.

Deliberately deferred — do not annotate high_cell10 yet. Full protocol:

  1. Keep tuning using the development set (high_cell9 + low_cell6), as normal.
  2. Once the recipe is genuinely settled, fold high_cell9 + low_cell6 into the training pool.
  3. Train the final/production checkpoint once, same recipe, on the enlarged pool.
  4. Only then annotate high_cell10 (python scripts/annotation/annotate.py --image-dir data/frames/02_unet_holdout/final_test --mask-dir data/masks/02_unet_holdout_multiclass --multiclass — note the explicit --image-dir/--mask-dir pair; a bare --pool 02_unet_holdout/final_test does not resolve the mask directory correctly).
  5. Evaluate the final checkpoint on high_cell10 exactly once. That's the reported blind-test score.

If asked to annotate or evaluate high_cell10 before step 2 has actually happened, that's very likely premature — confirm first.

Resolved 2026-09-10. high_cell10 was removed from 03_mask_factory on 2026-09-10 — it is the U-Net's blind test and must not also feed classifier training. The pool is now 608 frames across 12 cells, and those 12 are exactly the cells that feed 01_annotate_pool's domain-adapt frames. Its frames had been sitting there since the 2026-09-03 merge, from before its role changed.

docs.title: Train/val split (01_annotate_pool)
docs.text:
Split Frames % Role Train 371 ~90% U-Net training Val 54 ~10% Checkpoint selection / early stopping only — not the reportable score

There is no third "test" split inside 01_annotate_pool anymore (removed 2026-09-04, celldform.config.DataConfig/scripts/training/train_unet.py) — it was computed every run and printed in the split summary, but never actually built into a loader or evaluated by anything; the external 02_unet_holdout development/blind-test evaluation already fulfills the role a third split would have, so keeping one was pure redundancy that shrank the training pool for nothing. The current 90/10 split reuses what used to be a separate, unused 10% "test" allocation as val_split instead of the old dedicated 15% — net effect: the training pool grew from ~69% to ~90% of the annotated data with the same monitoring mechanics, just on a smaller slice.

docs.title: How the grouping works
docs.text:
Splitting is group-aware (scripts/training/train_unet.py::_build_groups/_group_split) — frames from the same cell or the same legacy acquisition burst never split across train/val, since they're correlated (same biology, same laser session). Two group types:

  • Legacy frames (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.jpg) are clustered into acquisition bursts — a gap of more than 5 seconds between sorted timestamps starts a new burst.
  • Domain-adapt frames (domain_<her2>_<cell_id>_<frame>.jpg) are grouped by cell identity.

At the current pool size (445 frames), this produces 22 groups: 11 legacy bursts (~17-20 frames each) and 11 domain cells (~19-24 frames each). The split algorithm shuffles group order (seeded, reproducible), then fills the val bucket with whole groups until it reaches the target frame count, with the remainder going to train — so split sizes approximate the configured ratio rather than hitting it exactly, since group sizes vary and a bucket only checks "have I reached target" before adding the next whole group (it can overshoot, never undershoot).

docs.title: Why internal validation was misleading
docs.text:
The single most consequential finding from the 2026-09 evaluation sweep, worth keeping visible here since it shapes why the three-tier terminology above exists at all:

The internal validation split tests generalization to unseen frames of already-trained-on cell identities — not to a genuinely novel cell. A checkpoint tuned to look excellent on it (bf32_reg2_cos, internal val DSC 0.862) scored only DSC 0.163 on the first genuinely held-out cell ever evaluated (high_cell9), while a "worse-looking" checkpoint (higher internal train/val gap, informally called "overfitting") scored 0.428 — roughly 2.6× better on real generalization despite scoring worse on the metric everything had been tuned against.

Root cause, once the full development set was evaluated: both high_cell9 and low_cell6's true trapped-cell size (704 / 886 px²) falls at or below every one of the 11 training cells' (825-1549 px²) — a real train/development-set size mismatch that the internal split, drawn from the same size distribution as training, could never surface. See Training Results for the full sweep, the per-cell breakdown, and what fixed it (partially).

Superseded figure (23 September 2026)

The 1549 px² upper bound above is high_cell1 as annotated at the time. That cell was re-annotated on 23 September and now measures 678 px² — the smallest cell in the study, not the largest. The old masks no longer exist. The size mismatch described here was real but smaller than stated, and part of the gap was an annotation artifact. Current ranges: training 688–1449 px², development set 678–1033 px², interleaved. See docs/status.md.

docs.title: Contamination firewall
docs.text:
• Legacy images carry no HER2 label — safe for U-Net training, cannot contaminate the classifier.
  • 02_unet_holdout's top level (high_cell9, low_cell6) was never used during U-Net training. It is used repeatedly during development, though — see the terminology table above; this is not the same guarantee as a blind test.
  • 02_unet_holdout/final_test/ (high_cell10) has never been evaluated against anything, and physically cannot be reached by any routine pool command until it's pointed at explicitly (see Cell roles). This is the one genuinely untouched pool.
  • 03_mask_factory cells were never part of 02_unet_holdout at any point and never will be. high_cell10 briefly sat in both after the 2026-09-03→09-04 role change; that was resolved on 2026-09-10 (see Cell roles) and the two pools now share no cell.

docs.title: Regenerating frames
docs.text:
celldform-organize-dataset                                    # defaults
celldform-organize-dataset --every-n 100 --domain-adapt-n 10  # denser sampling
celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean                          # skip wiping data/frames/

The full celldform-organize-dataset pipeline does not currently reproduce the 2026-09-04 cell reallocation

celldform/acquisition/organiser.py's _video_lists() has been updated so a fresh run would put high_cell10 in unet_test and low_cell5 in domain_adapt/inference correctly — but the current data on disk was fixed by hand (moving files, not rerunning the organiser) specifically to avoid re-touching 02_unet_holdout mid-annotation and re-decoding videos unnecessarily. Don't run celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean casually right now without checking it won't fight the manual final_test/ nesting — a full --clean rerun would rebuild everything correctly from scratch, but would also wipe existing annotations, which almost certainly isn't what you want mid-project.

docs.title: Demonstration application
docs.text:
Runs the trained models on a newly recorded video and reports the HER2 class of the trapped SKBR3 cell. Not real-time (a measured frame costs a network pass; the 45.5 ms camera interval is only a speed reference).

celldform-demo [recording]                          # the window (Windows installer: the desktop shortcut)
python -m celldform.demo.run <recording> --out <dir> --bundle models.zip      # headless
python -m celldform.demo.models make --unet w.pt --config c.yaml --classifier f.joblib --out models   # prepare the files

The app contains no models. On a new machine it cannot analyze anything until the required files are loaded; see Required files below, and Installing on Windows.

A recording folder holds video.avi and, if present, SKBR3.txt and frames.csv (per-frame laser log).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. source.py reads the video (a damaged tail ends the stream, it never raises), removes the burned-in overlay text, converts to gray 1228x922.
  2. Only the measured frames are decoded and segmented: in every 200-frame laser step, offsets 0, 20, 60, 100, 140, 180 (configs/analysis/features.yaml).
  3. segment.py: the U-Net you loaded (its crop and filters from its settings file) -> labels at full frame.
  4. analyze.py: trapped cell = region nearest the trap (learned from the frames seen so far, or set by a click), the five frame checks, shape and deformation features.
  5. session.py: laser steps accumulate; the framework classifier (step LR + LR on PC1 of the selected 4, equal-weight mean, 14/15 leave-one-cell-out) gives P(high) only with >= 80 % of measured frames passing and >= 3 laser steps. With >= 10 steps it is the full classifier; with 3 to 9 it is the step model alone, labelled short recording (see below). Otherwise the verdict is withheld with the reason.

Outputs of the headless run: annotated.mp4 (predicted mask outlined white, decoy grey), frames.csv, steps.csv, verdict.json (includes the caveats and timing).

docs.title: Caveats the app prints
docs.text:
• Masks come from the U-Net you loaded; the classifier's features were measured on nnU-Net masks.
  • A laser current range or hold time different from the training recordings (500-1200 mA) is reported from frames.csv.
  • The crop centre of the U-Net is a calibration of the training setup's trap; a recording from another setup needs --crop-center.

docs.title: Known limitation
docs.text: The app works on recordings made like the ones the models were trained on. On four recordings from a newer setup (colour camera, a 298-1000 mA ramp in steps of about 9 s instead of 500-1200 mA held for 30 s) the U-Net found the cell in only 2-13 % of the measured frames, so the app correctly gave no verdict; a different pre-processing or a model fine-tuned on frames of that setup is needed there. The dashboard shows why frames were rejected, which tells you whether a recording is the problem. See Project status.

docs.title: Required files (first run on a new machine)
docs.text:
Nothing is bundled with the program, so a new installation has to be given a segmentation model and the HER2 classifier before Analyze works (browsing a recording needs none). The segmentation model is either the U-Net weights with their settings file, or an nnU-Net checkpoint (or both). The Required files box lists the files with a mark each: ✔ loaded and checked, ✘ the file was refused (with the reason), ○ not loaded yet.

File What it is What is checked U-Net weights (.pt) the segmentation model it is a U-Net with 2 or 3 classes (width and classes are read from the weights); read with weights_only, so it cannot run code U-Net settings (.yaml) filters, crop size and crop centre the model was trained with every value is present, sensible and fits a 1228x922 frame; found automatically when unet_settings.yaml or config.yaml sits beside the weights nnU-Net checkpoint (.pth), instead of the two above one nnU-Net 2d checkpoint; nothing else is needed read safely (only tensors, plain values and NumPy numbers are accepted, so it cannot run code); a 2d model with one input channel and labels 0 = background, 1 = trapped cell; then run once on a blank frame HER2 classifier (.joblib) the fitted step model + cell model it contains only what a HER2 framework contains (everything else is refused unopened), and it expects the features this version measures Training-cell reference (.csv, optional) the 15 training cells' features has the columns the comparison chart needs; without it that chart says so

Which model runs. When both a U-Net and an nnU-Net are loaded, Segment with chooses; the nnU-Net is the default because it is the model the classifier's features were measured on (so the "masks are not from nnU-Net" caveat disappears). It is more accurate (per-cell Dice 0.94 against 0.87 for the U-Net in leave-one-cell-out testing) but slower: about 0.5 s a frame on a GPU and several seconds on a CPU, so a recording takes minutes instead of under a minute. A recording of a few hundred measured frames is fine on a GPU; on a PC without one the U-Net is the practical choice.

The nnU-Net file. nnU-Net normally wants a whole model folder; everything it needs is inside its .pth, so the app reads that one file and writes a stripped copy (without the optimizer state and training log, half the size, same predictions) into its cache folder the first time. It needs the nnunetv2 package, which the Windows installer includes and pip install "celldform[app]" installs; without it the row says so and the U-Net still works.

When the weights and their settings are both loaded they are run together once on a blank frame, which shows (and proves) that they work on this machine and which device (CPU or GPU) they use. The files you loaded are remembered (their paths and SHA-256 only) and checked again at the next start; one that has gone or changed is shown as ✘ rather than failing.

Model bundle. One folder or .zip that carries all of it, with a SHA-256 for every file, so a file damaged or swapped on the way is refused and nothing is half-loaded. Use Load a model bundle in the box. Whoever holds the trained files makes it once:

python -m celldform.demo.models make --unet unet_deploy.pt --config config.yaml --classifier her2_framework.joblib \
       [--nnunet checkpoint_final.pth] [--reference features_cells.csv] --description "U-Net + 15-cell framework" \
       --out models --zip models.zip
python -m celldform.demo.models verify models.zip

A bundle is rebuilt, not copied: the U-Net is re-saved as bare weights (no optimizer state, about a third of the size), the settings file is rebuilt from the few keys the app reads (a training config.yaml holds dataset paths and split details that do not belong on someone else's computer), and an nnU-Net checkpoint is re-saved without its optimizer state and training log (474 MB becomes about 240 MB). A bundle may carry the nnU-Net alone, the U-Net pair alone, or both. The description and the classifier's own record are refused if they contain an e-mail address or a path. A .zip is unpacked into the user's cache folder with protection against entries that try to write elsewhere, links, and zip bombs.

A .joblib file is a pickle, and a pickle can run code when it is opened. The loader therefore only accepts the ten classes a HER2 framework is made of and refuses anything else without opening it; celldform.demo.framework.load(path, trusted=True) is plain joblib.load for a file you made yourself.
