Command line: --bundle models.zip, or --unet-file w.pt --unet-config c.yaml --classifier f.joblib, or --nnunet-file model.pth --classifier f.joblib; with both models given, --use unet|nnunet chooses (default nnunet). Developers on a machine that has the repository's checkpoints can still use --segmenter unet|nnunet.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Under the video the window has three tabs (celldform/demo/dashboard.py); they fill in while the recording runs.

Tab Panel What it shows Process Laser protocol and what was measured set current over the video against the 500-1200 mA the classifier was trained on; each 200-frame step coloured green / amber / red / grey Process Frames passing the checks, per laser step pass rate per step against the 80% the classifier needs Process Why frames were rejected no cell near the trap, too far, uncertain boundary, size off typical, ... Evidence Cell shape across the laser ramp median area and aspect ratio of passing frames per step against the current Evidence Where this cell sits among the 15 training cells the cell on two of the classifier's selected features, with the training cells coloured by HER2 class Evidence The cell across laser steps a picture of the cell with its predicted outline, one per step Result and model Result HER2 class with a probability gauge (step model, cell model, average); without a verdict, what is still missing Result and model Run and model segmentation model and device, frames measured, time per frame (camera interval 45.5 ms is a reference only), classifier training record

Save dashboard image (toolbar) writes every page on one PNG; every run also writes dashboard.png into its results folder, including from the command line. Before a run the tabs already show the recording's laser protocol and the model card.

docs.title: Controls, frame source and log
docs.text:
• Analyze / Pause (Resume) / Stop are buttons at the top of the right-hand panel; Analyze is what runs the models (the Browse bar only looks). Pause holds the run before the next frame is read; Stop works while paused and keeps the results so far. Paused time is left out of the timings (verdict.json has paused_seconds).
  • Frames from: Video | Images (stills) in the toolbar (--source video|images on the command line). Images are the stills*/ folder of the recording, or any folder of images. With stills.csv each picture is placed at its video frame (video_frame is 1-based), so laser steps, times and the laser log are the same as for the video; frames that have no still are skipped, and unselected frames are never read, which is faster than decoding the video. Without the table the sorted file order is the frame index. The stills carry the same camera image and the same burned-in overlay as the video, so they do not segment any better (checked 2026-11-18).
  • Log is the fourth dashboard tab: model load, the settings and caveats, one line per measured frame (frame, laser step, segmentation time, PASS with area and aspect ratio or REJECT with the reason), a line whenever another laser step becomes usable (with what the verdict is then), pauses, and the result. The same lines are saved as inference.log in the results folder, also from the command line.

docs.title: Browsing a recording (no analysis)
docs.text:
The Browse the recording bar under the picture plays the video or steps through its still images (whichever Frames from says) without running any model.

Control What it does Play / Pause, space plays at the chosen speed (0.25x to 16x); follows the clock, so frames are skipped rather than slowed when decoding falls behind slider jump to any frame |< < > >|, Home / Left / Right / End first frame, back, forward, last frame step how far < and > move: 1, 10, 50 frames, 1 laser step (200 frames), or 1000 frames, to sample through a recording Hide overlay text inpaints the burned-in laser readout (the analysis always does)

The line under the slider gives the frame, time, laser step and set current of the frame on show. Browsing is switched off while a run is going, and back on when it ends.

Zoom and pan work on the picture at any time, also during a run and while paused: mouse wheel zooms at the cursor (up to 32x, real pixels from 3x), drag pans, double-click or Fit view shows the whole picture. The status bar shows the pixel under the cursor (x, y, gray). A trap marked with Click the cell is converted to analysis-frame pixels whatever the zoom or the size of the picture.

docs.title: Pause
docs.text: Pause holds the run before the next frame is read (not only after a measured one), the picture shows PAUSED and the status bar says Paused; zoom and pan still work. The window receives only the newest frame, dashboard snapshot and log lines in a batch, so a slow screen cannot build up a backlog of frames that keeps playing after Pause (that is what made Pause look broken: with a window slower than the models, the video ran on for seconds).

docs.title: Opening a recording
docs.text:
Open recording (toolbar menu, or drop on the window) takes three kinds of input:

  • Video file...: that one file, also when its folder holds many videos. A folder with one video behaves as before (frames.csv = laser log, the *.txt = notes). With several videos in a folder, a video only picks up sidecars named after it: <video name>.csv (laser log) and <video name>.txt (notes); otherwise there is no laser log and the app says so in its caveats.
  • Image files... (select several): exactly the pictures you choose. If they come from a stills*/ folder whose stills.csv lists them, each keeps its video frame number (so laser steps and the laser log line up, and a subset such as frames 600-1200 is analysed as steps 3-5); otherwise they are numbered in name order (img2 before img10). Frames from is then fixed to Images. The laser log is found in the recording folder when it holds one video.
  • Recording folder...: as before; with several videos in it the window asks which one to open, and a folder with only pictures is read as images.

Command line: python -m celldform.demo.run <folder | video.avi | img1.png img2.png ...> --out <dir>.

docs.title: Stages: what can be pressed when
docs.text:
One function (MainWindow._refresh_controls) decides this from two facts, whether a recording is loaded and what the analysis is doing, and runs after every change, so no stage can be left with a stale button.

Stage Analyze Pause Stop Browse bar, Open, Models, Frames from nothing loaded off (pressing it explains why) off off Open only loaded, idle (also after playing the video) on off off on analyzing off on on off paused off on, reads Resume on off stopping (until the thread has ended) off off off off
  • A failed open (wrong file, no stills) leaves the recording that was loaded usable; the Frames from box goes back to what it was.
  • A recording cannot be opened or changed while an analysis is running or paused (Stop first).
  • An error inside the analysis, or while starting it, returns the window to idle with Analyze enabled and the error in the status bar and the Log tab. Unexpected errors in the window do not close it.
  • tests/test_demo_states.py walks every stage, including random sessions of button presses with the invariants checked after each press.
  • import cv2 makes Qt look for OpenCV's own plugins, which can stop Qt from creating a window; main() undoes it.

docs.title: Short recordings and provisional verdicts
docs.text:
The classifier was validated (leave-one-cell-out 14/15, AUC 0.94) on whole recordings: 10 or more laser steps, and at least 80% of measured frames passing the five frame checks. The app treats a recording by its length:

Usable laser steps Result fewer than 3 no verdict (the reason says how many steps and seconds are needed) 3 to 9 a short-recording verdict: the step model alone, labelled SHORT RECORDING, STEP MODEL ONLY 10 or more the full classifier, an ordinary verdict

A laser step is 200 frames, 9.1 s, so 3 steps is about 27 s and 10 steps about 91 s. Why the short result is weaker: the per-cell measures (baseline length, volume change and so on) compare the end of the ramp with its first 10 steps and cannot be computed from fewer, so the cell-level half of the classifier is left out rather than filled with the training cells' median, which would pull every answer toward the middle. A recording that short also stays at the first, low laser powers, so the cell is barely loaded and the answer rests on its size and shape rather than on how it deforms. In a test that cut the 15 recordings short, the step model alone placed 11 to 12 of 15 cells correctly from 3 to 10 steps, no better than from the full ramp (11 of 15), and one cell is about 7 points; do not read a short result as the 14/15 of the full classifier. The recording must still pass the 80% frame check.

The short-recording label appears in the window (orange, Read with care:), on the dashboard (badge, and "cell model not used"), in verdict.json ("status": "short", "validated": false) and in the logs. No option is needed for it.

The Give a provisional verdict even if the checks fail box (command line: --provisional) also computes a verdict when the frame checks fail or there are fewer than 3 steps. It is opt-in, off by default, locked while a run is going, and everything it produces says so:

  • the window shows PROVISIONAL, not validated: HIGH HER2 (P high 0.52) in orange, with Not a HER2 result, because: and every reason (too few steps, too low a pass rate, cell-level measures that were missing and replaced by the training cells' median);
  • the dashboard result panel carries a PROVISIONAL: NOT VALIDATED badge and the reasons, and the saved dashboard image starts with the same words;
  • verdict.json has "status": "provisional" and "validated": false; the log and inference.log say PROVISIONAL, NOT VALIDATED;
  • with no usable step at all (nothing passed) there is still no verdict, and a recording that does pass validation gets an ordinary verdict whatever the box says.

The 14/15 figure does not apply to a provisional verdict, and neither does any claim about accuracy. Example: on a recording of a low-HER2 cell where only 13 % of the measured frames passed the checks, the provisional verdict was high with P = 0.52 (step model 0.54, cell model 0.51): a coin flip that happened to land on the wrong side. Do not read anything into such a number.

docs.title: Window size, Maximize and full screen
docs.text: The window opens at a size that fits the screen. When it is wide enough (maximized, or full screen) it switches to a wide arrangement: the picture takes the whole height on the left and the controls and the dashboard share the right, so a big screen is used instead of showing black bars; smaller windows keep the stacked arrangement. The switch keeps everything (frame, tab, log, zoom). Maximize keeps the system's title bar, as on any window; F11 goes to true full screen (F11 or Esc to leave).

docs.title: Which stages use the GPU?
docs.text:
Only Stage 3 (U-Net segmentation) runs on the GPU. All other stages run entirely on CPU.

Stage Component GPU 1 — Acquisition FrameExtractor — OpenCV frame decode No 2 — Preprocessing PreprocessingPipeline — OpenCV / NumPy No 3 — Segmentation UNet, SegmentationTrainer — PyTorch Yes 3 — Inference UNet forward pass (also in the desktop app) Yes (or CPU, slower) 4 — Features MorphologyExtractor — scikit-image / NumPy No 5 — Classification CellClassifier — scikit-learn SVM/RF/DT No 6 — Biomechanics DeformationAnalyzer — scipy / NumPy No

docs.title: Device configuration
docs.text:
The device is auto-detected at runtime everywhere using:

device = conf.device or ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")

docs.title: Via configs/default.yaml
docs.text:
device: null     # auto-detect (default — uses CUDA if available)
device: "cuda"   # force GPU
device: "cpu"    # force CPU

docs.title: Via CLI flag
docs.text:
Training takes the device from the config only (celldform-train-unet has no --device). Inference and the single-frame check accept an override:

celldform-infer --video data/videos/experiment_01.mp4 --unet-ckpt checkpoints/unet_best.pt --device cpu
celldform-predict-single-frame --checkpoint checkpoints/unet_best.pt --frame <frame.png> --device cpu

docs.title: Checking GPU availability
docs.text:
import torch
print(torch.cuda.is_available())       # True / False
print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))   # e.g. "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080"
print(torch.cuda.memory_allocated())   # bytes currently in use

docs.title: Memory considerations
docs.text:
The U-Net processes (B, 1, 256, 256) float32 tensors. Approximate GPU memory usage at different batch sizes:

Batch size ~VRAM 8 ~1 GB 16 ~2 GB 32 ~4 GB

Reduce training.batch_size in configs/default.yaml if you run out of VRAM.

docs.title: Windows / WSL2
docs.text:
On WSL2, CUDA is supported via the NVIDIA CUDA on WSL2 driver. Verify with:

nvidia-smi
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"

Set training.num_workers: 0 on Windows to avoid DataLoader multiprocessing issues.

docs.title: HPC Guide (SLURM)
docs.text:
Running celldform U-Net training on a SLURM cluster. The job scripts were written and used on a university cluster with Tesla V100 GPUs; the table and settings below describe that cluster, so adjust the partition, modules and CUDA build for yours.

Node one machine that is both login and compute node Partitions standard (default), gpu — both on the same node, no time limit GPUs 3× Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB (driver 580, CUDA ≤ 13) CPU / RAM 80 cores, ~500 GB Account / QOS not required

V100, not A100

The V100 has FP16 tensor cores but no BF16 and no TF32. training.use_amp: true uses FP16 autocast plus a GradScaler (celldform/segmentation/trainer.py), which is what the V100 accelerates, so leave it on. Epoch times measured earlier on other hardware do not carry over; time a short run before sizing --time.

docs.title: Recommended Workflow
docs.text: Step Where Annotate masks Local machine (scripts/annotation/annotate.py) Preprocess frames Local machine (scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks) Upload preprocessed data rsync/scp to the cluster Clone code, create conda env cluster login shell Train / evaluate cluster, sbatch scripts/hpc/{training,evaluation}/*.sh (V100) Download checkpoint rsync/scp from the cluster Inference, evaluation, biomechanics Local machine (or the cluster)

docs.title: Step 1 — Clone the Code
docs.text:
cd ~/projects                        # or wherever you keep the project
git clone https://github.com/oppongbaah/cancer_cell_deformation.git
cd cancer_cell_deformation
mkdir -p logs/hpc                    # SLURM writes job logs here and will not create it

docs.title: Step 2 — Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
Use the cluster's Anaconda module and the celldform conda env (once, on the login node):

module load Anaconda3/2025.06-1
conda create -n celldform python=3.11 -y     # skip if it already exists (conda env list)
conda activate celldform
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126   # FIRST -- see below
pip install -e ".[hpc]"    # core deps incl. nnunetv2 (needs Python >= 3.10) + mpi4py

# Verify (the GPUs are visible on the login node too)
python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"
nnUNetv2_train -h

Notes for this cluster:

  • Batch jobs don't run your ~/.bashrc, so the job script loads the module itself and sources $EBROOTANACONDA3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh before running conda activate celldform.
  • Install torch from the cu126 index. The default PyPI wheel is now built for CUDA 13 (+cu130), which has no kernels for the V100 (compute capability 7.0; cu130 starts at 7.5). It installs fine, then warns "does not include kernels for this GPU" and fails on the first CUDA op. The cu126 build includes sm_70. To check: python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.get_arch_list())" must list sm_70. If a later pip install pulls in a +cu130 torch again, reinstall the same version from cu126: pip uninstall -y torch torchvision && pip install torch==<ver> torchvision==<ver> --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126.
  • Don't build the env on the PyTorch/2.9.1-CUDA-12.6.0 module: nnunetv2 excludes torch 2.9.x (torch!=2.9.*). Let pip choose torch; its wheels bundle the CUDA runtime, and the driver (580) supports it.
  • Every script in scripts/training/ and scripts/evaluation/ is Python, and the ones that chain others (train_experiment.py, train_cv_fold.py, ...) run each step with whichever python launched them. python scripts/... therefore uses the conda env on the cluster and .venv locally, with nothing to configure.

docs.title: Step 3 — Upload Preprocessed Data
docs.text:
From your local machine:

rsync -avP data/preprocessed/ YOUR_USERNAME@CLUSTER_HOST:~/projects/cancer_cell_deformation/data/preprocessed/

Only preprocessed/ is needed. Do not upload data/raw/, which holds the large videos and is not used in training.

docs.title: Step 4 — Check Paths in the Config
docs.text:
Data paths in configs/*.yaml are relative to the repo root, so they work unchanged as long as the job runs from there (both the batch script and celldform-hpc-submit do). The settings that matter on the cluster:

device: cuda

training:
  num_workers: 8   # match --cpus-per-task; beyond 16 adds no throughput
  batch_size: 32   # a V100 has 32 GB; raise once you have >= 100 annotated masks
  use_amp: true    # FP16 autocast on V100 tensor cores

Reproducibility across runs

training.cudnn_benchmark (default true, matching PyTorch's own default) trades reproducibility for speed by re-timing convolution kernels against runtime hardware state. It was verified locally to make same-seed reruns land on different results even with cudnn_deterministic: true also set (the runs differed between reruns). This has not been re-verified on the cluster's V100s. If you need a run to be reproducible, set cudnn_benchmark: false explicitly.

docs.title: Step 5 — Submit Jobs
docs.text:
Every training and evaluation script has a SLURM job script under scripts/hpc/, mirroring scripts/training/ and scripts/evaluation/. Submit from the repo root. Arguments after the script name are passed straight to the underlying script:

sbatch scripts/hpc/training/train_unet.sh                                       # configs/default.yaml
sbatch scripts/hpc/training/train_unet.sh --config configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml --seed 43
sbatch scripts/hpc/training/train_experiment.sh postswap/experiment_1b_loss e1b_lovasz_s42
sbatch --array=1-5 scripts/hpc/training/train_cv_fold.sh randswap/experiment_0_cv_baseline cv_baseline
sbatch scripts/hpc/evaluation/eval_native.sh --checkpoint CK --config CFG --log results/<exp>/eval_log_native.jsonl
sbatch scripts/hpc/evaluation/summarize_cv.sh --exp randswap/experiment_0_cv_baseline --run cv_baseline
Job script Runs Partition Resources (default) training/train_unet.sh scripts/training/train_unet.py (no args → --config configs/default.yaml) gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 12 h training/distill_ensemble.sh scripts/training/distill_ensemble.py gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 12 h training/train_experiment.sh scripts/training/train_experiment.py <experiment> <run> [train args]: train + score gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 12 h training/train_cv_fold.sh scripts/training/train_cv_fold.py <experiment> <run> <fold>; under --array the fold is the array index gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 12 h training/train_deploy_model.sh scripts/training/train_deploy_model.py <experiment> <run> gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 12 h training/train_nnunet_cv.sh scripts/training/train_nnunet_cv.py (--setup once first) gpu 1 V100, 16 CPU, 64 GB, 72 h training/train_student_cv.sh scripts/training/train_student_cv.py gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 48 h evaluation/evaluate_unet.sh scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 2 h evaluation/eval_native.sh scripts/evaluation/eval_native.py gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 2 h evaluation/eval_testing_set.sh scripts/evaluation/eval_testing_set.py <ckpt> <config> <log> [pool] gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 2 h evaluation/ensemble_eval.sh scripts/evaluation/ensemble_eval.py gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 2 h evaluation/eval_ensemble_cv.sh scripts/evaluation/eval_ensemble_cv.py gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 64 GB, 8 h evaluation/latency_benchmark.sh scripts/evaluation/latency_benchmark.py (add --exclusive for publishable timings) gpu 1 V100, 8 CPU, 32 GB, 2 h evaluation/eval_nnunet.sh scripts/evaluation/eval_nnunet.py standard 4 CPU, 16 GB, 1 h evaluation/summarize_cv.sh scripts/evaluation/summarize_cv.py standard 4 CPU, 16 GB, 30 min evaluation/compare_postswap.sh scripts/evaluation/compare_postswap.py standard 4 CPU, 16 GB, 30 min evaluation/check_convergence.sh scripts/evaluation/check_convergence.py standard 4 CPU, 16 GB, 30 min

The old run_postswap.sh <run> is gone. Use train_experiment.sh postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline <run>.

Override resources at submit time without editing a file, e.g. sbatch --time=24:00:00 --mem=64G .... sbatch --test-only <job script> validates the request without submitting. Every job sources scripts/hpc/_common.sh, which activates the celldform conda env (--export=ALL,CONDA_ENV=<name> for another) and prints the job's GPU and torch build.

Logs. Each job leaves one log in logs/hpc/: <job-name>_<jobid>.out when it exits 0, or <job-name>_<jobid>.err when it fails, times out or is cancelled. On failure the whole log (stdout and stderr interleaved, in order) becomes the .err, so the error is in it whichever stream printed it, and a closing job FAILED (exit N) line gives the exit code (143 = cancelled or time limit). ls logs/hpc/*.err lists the failures.

Finished jobs are filed by experiment afterwards (git mv), one folder each: nnunet1000_5fold/, loocv_unet/, loocv_nnunet/ (setup, 15 rounds, summary, deploy), anvil_unet/. New jobs still land in logs/hpc/ itself (SLURM will not create a missing folder); the code that reads a job log searches the subfolders too. Failed attempts that were rerun are deleted (they stay in the git history).

Auto-commit. When a job exits 0, scripts/hpc/_autocommit.sh commits its outputs and pushes them to the current branch on GitHub. When a job fails, is cancelled or times out, it commits and pushes only that job's .err (commit run: <job> FAILED (exit N, job <id>), with the error lines in the message), so failures show up on GitHub; a failed run's partial outputs are never committed.

  • What is committed: that job's logs/hpc/<job>_<jobid>.out, plus results/ and logs/ as far as .gitignore admits them (eval logs *.jsonl, training logs *.log). Figures, CSVs and checkpoints stay out. Code is never committed by a job, and anything else you have staged or edited is left as it is (git commit --only).
  • Where: the current branch, never main/master (on those it does nothing). Jobs finishing together commit one at a time (a lock in .git/).
  • How it pushes: over SSH with the repo's deploy key ~/.ssh/celldform_deploy (GitHub → repo Settings → Deploy keys, write access). Your own remote and credentials are not used. If a push fails, the commit stays local and the job still succeeds; push it yourself.
  • Record: one line per job in logs/hpc/autocommit.log (not tracked), e.g. committed 55a2b28 on feat-hpc and pushed.
  • Switches: sbatch --export=ALL,AUTOCOMMIT=0 ... skips it; AUTOCOMMIT_PUSH=0 commits without pushing.

celldform-hpc-submit generates the train_unet job on the fly and submits it (same setup, via _common.sh):

celldform-hpc-submit --config configs/default.yaml
celldform-hpc-submit --config configs/default.yaml --time 24:00:00 --dry-run   # print, don't submit

Defaults: --partition gpu --time 12:00:00 --cpus 8 --gpus 1 --mem 32G --conda-env celldform, no account or QOS (pass --account/--qos only if your cluster requires them).

Monitoring (SLURM accounting was disabled on this cluster, so sacct returned nothing; use the logs):

squeue -u $USER                                   # queued/running status
squeue -u $USER --start                           # estimated start time, if SLURM has computed one
scontrol show job <jobid>                         # details while it is queued/running
tail -f logs/hpc/<job-name>_<jobid>.out           # live output; the last line gives the exit code
ls logs/hpc/*.err                                 # which jobs failed
scancel <jobid>                                   # cancel

The node has 3 V100s, so up to three single-GPU jobs (e.g. three seeds or CV folds) run side by side.

docs.title: Step 6 — Download the Checkpoint
docs.text:
From your local machine:

rsync -avP YOUR_USERNAME@CLUSTER_HOST:~/projects/cancer_cell_deformation/checkpoints/ checkpoints/

docs.title: Iterative Training Cycle
docs.text:
Local                              Cluster
─────────────────────              ──────────────────────────────────
scripts/annotation/annotate.py
scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py
                      rsync data/preprocessed/ ──►
                                  sbatch scripts/hpc/training/train_unet.sh
                      ◄── rsync checkpoints/
scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py

Repeat after each annotation batch. Target DSC ≥ 0.80 before freezing the model.

docs.title: Installing the desktop app
docs.text: celldform's desktop app opens a recording of a trapped cell, runs the models and shows the HER2 class with the evidence behind it. It works offline and sends nothing anywhere (Privacy).

docs.title: Do I need to install the library first?
docs.text:
No, not for the Windows installer. The installer is self-contained: Python and every library the app needs are inside it, so you do not need to install Python, pip or the celldform library beforehand. Just run the installer.

You only need Python and the library if you choose the second route below.

A. Windows installer B. Python (pip) Who it is for someone who just wants to analyze recordings someone who also wants the library, scripts or other systems What you must install first nothing Python 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12 How run celldform-setup-<version>.exe pip install "celldform[app]" How you start it the desktop shortcut or Start Menu celldform-demo (and celldform-shortcut for a desktop icon) Size large (it contains PyTorch) the libraries are downloaded by pip

Both routes need the same thing before the app can analyze anything: the model files (see First start). They are not part of either install.

docs.title: A. The Windows installer
docs.text:
1. Run celldform-setup-<version>.exe. It installs for you only, so no administrator rights are needed.
  2. On the "Select Additional Tasks" page leave Create a desktop shortcut ticked (and tick Add to the Start Menu if you like), then install. Start celldform from the shortcut.
  3. If Windows SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", the installer is not code-signed. Check that the SHA-256 of the file you downloaded equals the one you were given (Get-FileHash celldform-setup-<version>.exe in PowerShell), then choose More info → Run anyway.

For several computers at once: celldform-setup-<version>.exe /SILENT /TASKS="desktopicon".

docs.title: B. Python (pip)
docs.text:
Needs Python 3.10, 3.11 or 3.12. In a terminal:

python -m venv celldform-env
celldform-env\Scripts\activate           # Linux/macOS: source celldform-env/bin/activate
pip install "celldform[app]"             # the library and the app (PySide6)
celldform-demo                           # starts the app
celldform-shortcut                       # optional: a desktop shortcut (--start-menu, --remove)

Until the package is on PyPI, install from a clone of the repository instead: pip install -e ".[app]" inside it. pip install celldform alone (without [app]) gives the library without the window.

docs.title: First start: load the files
docs.text:
The app contains no models. The right-hand panel, Required files, lists what it needs, each marked ○ (not loaded):

File What it is U-Net weights (.pt) and U-Net settings (.yaml) the segmentation model, and how frames are prepared for it or nnU-Net checkpoint (.pth) the segmentation model, as one file (the more accurate, slower one) HER2 classifier (.joblib) the fitted classifier

You need one segmentation model (the U-Net pair, or the nnU-Net; both can be loaded and you choose) plus the classifier. Until then, Analyze stays grey and its tooltip says what is missing. You can already open a recording and browse it (play, step, zoom).

Where do the files come from? From whoever trained the models; the project does not distribute them. Ask for a model bundle, one .zip that holds them all.

Easiest: Load a model bundle ▾ → Bundle .zip file… and pick the .zip. Every file inside is checked against its checksum and the marks turn ✔. Or load the files one by one with each row's Load… button (the settings file is found by itself when it sits next to the weights). A wrong file is refused with the reason, and what was loaded before stays loaded.

The app remembers which files you loaded and checks them again at the next start, so this is a one-time step. Clear all forgets them (the files themselves are never deleted or changed).

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
1. Open recording ▾: a video file, several image files, or a recording folder (or drop them on the window).
  2. Browse with the bar under the picture; zoom with the mouse wheel, pan by dragging, F11 for full screen.
  3. Analyze, then Pause / Resume / Stop as needed. The dashboard and the Log tab fill in as it runs.
  4. Open results folder (or Documents\celldform\results): each analysis writes a folder named after the recording and the time, with verdict.json, frames.csv, steps.csv, dashboard.png and inference.log. They do not say which folder the recording came from or who ran it.

The app gives a verdict only when a recording has at least 3 usable laser steps (about 27 s) and 80 % of the measured frames pass the checks; otherwise it says why. From 10 steps (about 91 s) it uses the full validated classifier; shorter recordings get a result labelled as a short recording, from the step model alone. Details, and the optional provisional verdict, are in the demonstration app.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Windows installer: Settings → Apps → celldform → Uninstall. It asks whether to also delete the saved settings (the list of model files); your results in Documents\celldform are never deleted, and neither are the model files you loaded. pip: pip uninstall celldform, then delete celldform-env and, if you made one, the desktop shortcut (celldform-shortcut --remove).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: What you see What it means Analyze is grey A recording is not open, or a required file is not loaded: the tooltip says which. ✘ next to a file The reason is shown under its name: wrong kind of file, damaged, settings that do not fit, or a classifier trained on other features. "does not match its SHA-256" The bundle changed or was damaged in transit: copy or download it again. "not part of a HER2 classifier; the file was not opened" The .joblib contains something a classifier never contains. Do not use it. "the U-Net and its settings do not work together" The .pt and .yaml come from different models, or the graphics driver failed. celldform-demo is not found The environment is not active (run the activate line again), or you installed without [app]. No window opens Run celldform-demo --selftest (or celldform.exe --selftest for the installer); it prints what failed.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text: The celldform pipeline is strictly linear — each stage's output is the next stage's input. Stages 2 and 3 are independent: preprocessing has no knowledge of the U-Net architecture, and the U-Net receives already-preprocessed images.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Stage 1           Stage 2              Stage 3          Stage 4              Stage 5             Stage 6           Stage 7
──────────────    ─────────────────    ─────────────    ─────────────────    ───────────────     ─────────────     ─────────────────
Acquisition   →  Preprocessing    →   U-Net        →  Feature          →   Classification  →   Biomechanics  →   Desktop app
                 (separate stage)     Segmentation     Extraction                               Analysis          (celldform.demo)

FrameExtractor   PreprocessingPipeline UNet             MorphologyExtractor  CellClassifier      DeformationAnalyzer HER2Framework + CellSession
acquisition/     preprocessing/        segmentation/    features/            classification/     biomechanics/     demo/

docs.title: Stage 1 — Acquisition
docs.text:
Module: celldform/acquisition/extractor.py

FrameExtractor reads an optical tweezer video and writes greyscale frames as PNGs to disk. Two temporal sampling modes:

  • every_n — keep every N-th frame
  • target_fps — resample to a fixed rate

Trapped-cell detection uses three physics-based cues applied in sequence:

  1. Spatial channel filter — only blobs in the central channel_width fraction of the image
  2. Circularity filter — 4π·area/perimeter² ≥ min_circularity
  3. Darkest blob wins — trapped cells appear dark against the bright channel background

Each video produces a <stem>_manifest.csv recording frame index, timestamp, centroid, and displacement per saved frame.

change_threshold for optical tweezers

Set change_threshold=None for all optical tweezer experiments. The cell is trapped and does not translate — deformation is shape change, not position change. A non-null threshold will filter out all frames.

docs.title: Stage 2 — Preprocessing
docs.text:
Module: celldform/preprocessing/pipeline.py

PreprocessingPipeline is a callable that converts a raw greyscale uint8 frame to a float32 array in [0, 1] at (256, 256).

Fixed operation order:

Step Operation Purpose 1 Median filter (median_kernel=3) Remove salt-and-pepper noise 2 CLAHE (clip_limit=2.0, tile_grid=8×8) Equalise contrast under uneven illumination 3 Morphological open → close Remove bright specks; fill dark gaps 4 Bicubic resize to (256, 256) Match U-Net input size 5 Min-max normalise to [0, 1] float32 Stable gradient flow

Each step can be toggled individually via the enabled dict for ablation experiments.

Preprocessing is manual

Preprocessing is not applied inside the training loop. Run scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks before training. See Workflow Guide.

docs.title: Stage 3 — U-Net Segmentation
docs.text:
Module: celldform/segmentation/unet.py, celldform/segmentation/trainer.py

UNet implements the Ronneberger et al. (2015) encoder–decoder with BatchNorm + ReLU.

Component Detail Input (B, 1, H, W) float32 preprocessed frame (256×256 by default) Encoder 4 blocks — 64 → 128 → 256 → 512 channels Bottleneck 1024 channels Decoder 4 blocks with skip connections Output (B, out_channels, H, W) raw logit map

Note

forward() returns raw logits — sigmoid/softmax is not applied internally. Use model.predict() for thresholded/argmax masks. out_channels=1 (default, BCEWithLogitsLoss in the trainer) is the frozen binary pipeline contract; out_channels>1 is an opt-in multiclass mode (CrossEntropyLoss + softmax/argmax), set via unet.out_channels in the config.

Training uses combined BCE + Dice loss in binary mode (out_channels=1):

Loss = α × BCE(pos_weight) + (1 − α) × Dice
Parameter Default Purpose loss_alpha 0.3 BCE weight — Dice carries 70% of the signal loss_pos_weight 100.0 Upweights cell pixels in BCE to counter ~550:1 background/cell imbalance

Both are set in configs/default.yaml under training. In multiclass mode (out_channels>1), a Dice + Cross-Entropy loss (_DiceCELoss) is used instead, with an optional per-class training.class_weights list (e.g. [1.0, 3.0, 3.0]) in place of loss_pos_weight — CrossEntropyLoss's weighted-mean reduction renormalises by weight mass, so these weights are not directly comparable in magnitude to loss_pos_weight. The best checkpoint is saved by validation DSC — always the primary/trapped-cell class, so it's comparable between binary and multiclass runs. Supports ReduceLROnPlateau, cosine, or no scheduler.

Class imbalance

Cancer cells occupy roughly 0.18% of a 256×256 frame (~118 pixels out of 65,536). Without pos_weight, the BCE loss is dominated by background pixels and the model learns to ignore the cell entirely. pos_weight=100 tells BCE to treat each cell pixel as if it were 100 background pixels. Increase it if recall is low; decrease it if precision is low and recall is near 1.0.

Multiclass evaluation

SegmentationTrainer.evaluate() returns a flat metrics dict in binary mode, or a dict keyed by class id (plus "mean") in multiclass mode — see SegmentationMetrics.per_class(). scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py and Visualizer.plot_training_curves() both handle either shape.

GPU: The U-Net is the only stage that runs on the GPU. See GPU & Hardware.

docs.title: Stage 4 — Feature Extraction
docs.text:
Module: celldform/features/extractor.py

MorphologyExtractor takes a binary mask and returns 15 morphological descriptors per cell. The largest connected region above min_area_px=50 is used.

Feature Description area Cell area (px² or μm² if calibrated) perimeter Boundary length major_axis, minor_axis Ellipse fit axes aspect_ratio major / minor — primary deformation signal eccentricity Ellipse eccentricity circularity 4π·area / perimeter² solidity area / convex-hull area hu_0 – hu_6 Log-scaled Hu moment invariants

Feature ordering

Features fed to the classifier must be sorted alphabetically by name — the same order sorted(features.keys()) produces. Do not change this without updating RealTimePipeline and scripts/inference/infer.py.

docs.title: Stage 5 — Classification
docs.text:
Module: celldform/classification/classifiers.py

CellClassifier wraps an RBF-kernel SVM inside CalibratedClassifierCV for probability output.

Label Meaning 0 Low HER2 expression (stiffer cell) 1 High HER2 expression (more deformable)

The thesis requires comparative analysis of SVM, RF, and DT. All classifiers implement the same interface (fit, predict, predict_proba, evaluate, save, load) so they can be swapped without changes to inference scripts.

Class imbalance

Training set is ~64 % high / 36 % low. Always use class_weight='balanced' and cell-level cross-validation (leave-one-cell-out), not frame-level.

docs.title: Stage 6 — Biomechanics
docs.text:
Module: celldform/biomechanics/analysis.py

DeformationAnalyzer computes the rate of deformation (RoD) — the linear slope of a chosen morphological metric (default: aspect_ratio) over the experiment time axis.

Key methods:

  • sliding_rate() — windowed local RoD estimate
  • analyze_batch() — aggregate mean RoD and peak deformation across multiple experiments
  • optical_correlation() — Pearson and Spearman correlations between laser power / trap current and deformation outcome (directly answers the thesis research question)
  • fit_kelvin_voigt() — fits σ = E·ε + η·dε/dt to estimate Young's modulus E and viscosity η

docs.title: Stage 7 — Desktop app
docs.text:
Module: celldform/demo/

The desktop application (celldform-demo) runs the trained models over a recorded video or image sequence and reports the HER2 class of the trapped cell, with the evidence behind it. It reads the recording, measures a fixed sample of frames (offsets 0, 20, 60, 100, 140 and 180 in every 200-frame laser step), applies the five frame checks, accumulates the laser steps, and gives a verdict only when at least 3 steps are usable and 80 % of the measured frames pass; otherwise it says why. With 10 or more steps it is the full validated classifier; with 3 to 9 it is the step model alone, labelled as a short recording. The classifier is the final framework (step-level logistic regression plus a cell-level model on the first principal component of four features, equal-weight mean).

It is not real-time and not connected to the instrument: it analyses recordings, and a measured frame costs a network pass (about 40 ms for the U-Net on a modern GPU, against the camera's 45.5 ms frame interval, which is only a speed reference). See the demonstration app; the older per-frame helper in celldform.integration is described in Per-frame inference (legacy).

docs.title: Privacy: what stays on your computer
docs.text: celldform sends nothing anywhere. It has no account, no update check, no analytics and no crash reporting, and it works with the network cable unplugged.

docs.title: How that is enforced
docs.text:
• At start the program switches off network access for itself: any attempt to reach another computer raises an error, even from a library it uses (connections to the same machine, which Qt and Python itself use, stay allowed). Telemetry switches of the libraries it contains are set off. tests/test_demo_privacy.py checks this, and that a full analysis works with the network blocked.
  • The installer installs the program only: no models, no data, no background service, nothing that starts with Windows.
  • The build refuses to produce an installer that carries its maker's data: installer/audit_package.py searches everything that would ship for the maker's e-mail address, GitHub name and user name, the build computer's home folder (compiled Python files remember it, so the build runs in a neutral folder), access tokens, private keys, and data files (models, checkpoints, videos, tables, results, logs).

docs.title: What the program writes, and where
docs.text:
What Where Contains Settings %APPDATA%\celldform\settings.json the paths and SHA-256 of the model files you loaded, the last folder, nothing else Results Documents\celldform\results\<time>_<recording>\ the analysis of one recording: verdict, per-frame and per-step tables, dashboard picture, log Unpacked bundles %LOCALAPPDATA%\celldform\Cache\bundles the files of a .zip bundle you loaded Prepared nnU-Net %LOCALAPPDATA%\celldform\Cache\nnunet a stripped copy of an nnU-Net checkpoint you loaded (no optimizer state), so it loads fast next time; safe to delete

Result files are written so they can be shared: the recording is named by its file name only, the log never contains the folder it came from, and your home folder, user name and e-mail addresses are replaced (~, <user>, <email>). Set CELLDFORM_HOME to a folder to keep settings and results there instead (for example on a USB stick).

docs.title: What you should still decide yourself
docs.text:
• The videos and the model files are yours; the program never copies them. A model bundle carries only weights, a small settings file and the classifier, never the training data or the training configuration.
  • A .joblib classifier is a kind of file that can contain code. The program opens only the ten kinds of object a HER2 classifier consists of and refuses the rest unopened, but still load model files only from a source you trust, and compare the SHA-256 you were given.

docs.title: Research log: segmentation, September 2026
docs.text:
Historical record, not the current state

This page is the project's status as of 17–23 September 2026, kept as a record of how the segmentation work developed (run-to-run variance, the per-cell collapse, why the evaluation changed). Later work replaced its protocol (random whole-cell cross-validation, a 384 px native crop, nnU-Net, the classifier and the desktop app). For where the project stands now, read Project status.

docs.title: Current model
docs.text:
checkpoints/postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline/postswap_ftl_cw142_s42/unet_best.pt · config configs/postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline/postswap_ftl_cw142_s42.yaml

Focal–Tversky loss (α 0.7, β 0.3, γ 0.75, Abraham & Khan 2019) · class weights [1, 4, 2] · width 64 · cosine · scale augmentation only · 451-frame pool.

Development set (4 cells, 203 annotated frames, fully annotated 23 September):

evaluated DSC spread single model, 4-seed mean 0.809 sd 0.049 ensemble of four 0.859 —

Two of four runs collapse on a single cell — a different cell each time

run worst cell its DSC internal val convergence check s42 low-6 0.718 0.9327 passed s43 low-6 0.804 0.9398 passed s44 high-1 0.507 0.9050 FLAGGED s45 high-9 0.630 0.9357 passed ✗

Neither cell size (high-1 678 px, high-9 704 px) nor internal validation predicts which cell goes. check_convergence.py caught s44 — behind on three of four cells — and missed s45, which trained normally and then lost one cell. Passing it is not evidence.

Ensembling is what fixes this. No per-cell collapse survives averaging: high-1 never falls below 0.823, high-9 never below 0.822.

high-1 high-9 low-5 low-6 All cells single model, 4-seed mean 0.742 0.792 0.890 0.770 0.809 ensemble of 4 0.823 0.848 0.920 0.818 0.859

But an ensemble is an inference-time construct, not a model — no checkpoint, 4× GPU, and the per-frame helper takes one UNet. Averaging the weights instead gives DSC 0.000: independently seeded networks sit in different loss basins and their hidden units are not aligned. Distillation — training one model on the ensemble's soft outputs — is the route to a single deployable checkpoint, and is not yet done.

docs.title: What changed on 17 September
docs.text:
The evaluation roster was restructured. high-10 moved into training and high-1 into the development set, because the development cells were measurably smaller than the training cells and the model was being judged on cells smaller than anything it had trained on.

Measured now, training spans 688–1449 px and the development set 678–1033 px, and the two interleave rather than separating: high-10 (688) sits between high-1 (678) and high-9 (704) — the intended effect.

Correction, 23 September

high-1 was re-annotated when its remaining frames were completed, and now measures 678 px, not the 1549 px recorded while it was a training cell. It is the smallest cell in the study, not the largest. The earlier masks no longer exist, so the annotations cannot be compared directly.

This weakens the premise above: the pre-exchange claim that every development cell was smaller than every training cell assumed a training minimum of 824 px, which depended on high-1 being large. The size gap was real but smaller than reported, and part of it was an annotation artifact. The effect on the two cells that did not move is measured directly and does not depend on it.

The effect on the two cells that did not move, and so remain comparable:

Cell before after high-9 0.600 0.845 ± 0.043 +0.245 — well outside the noise low-6 0.749 0.766 ± 0.044 inside the noise

One caveat on that result

high_cell10 (688 px) and high_cell9 (704 px) are near-twins — same laser regime, nearly the same size. Moving high-10 into training was close to adding a duplicate of high-9, so 0.845 is likely optimistic as an estimate for a genuinely new high-power cell. The mechanism is real; the effect size will not transfer intact.

Run-to-run variance was measured for the first time, and it is large — see the Workflow Guide rules and the banner on Training Results.

The loss function was ruled out as the bottleneck. Three interventions — class-weight rebalancing, excluding background from the Dice term, and replacing Dice with Focal–Tversky — produced 0.676, 0.675 and 0.691 against a 0.668 baseline. A structural finding along the way: the objective is 0.3·CE + 0.7·Dice, and class_weights reaches only the CE term, so that knob was never touching 70% of the loss.

docs.title: Where the evidence points
docs.text: Object scale, not hyperparameters. At 256×256 the trapped cell occupies 41–90 px — roughly a 6×6 to 9×9 blob — and the decoy class on high-10 about 51 px. That is very likely why no loss function recovered the decoy class: the information may not survive the 17× downsample. Resolution has not been revisited since the 128→256 ablation (+0.048, on 40 masks); the pool is now 451.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
1. Decide what the deployed model is — ensemble (0.859, no checkpoint, 4× GPU) or a distilled single model. This determines which number the thesis reports as "the model".
  2. Test resolution (384, then 512 if the trend holds), with a matched-batch-size control. The development set is now complete, so the baseline it is measured against is final.
  3. Understand the per-cell collapse — the largest single source of uncertainty in every number above, and nothing currently predicts it.
  4. The deferred optimizer and validation-split experiments, gated behind a multi-seed baseline.
  5. nnU-Net benchmark if the above fall short. Note its default loss is Dice+CE — i.e. this project's baseline — so any margin will come from architecture and schedule.

docs.title: Scripts Reference
docs.text:
Every script here, except the SLURM job scripts (hpc/), the one-off migrations (maintenance/) and the thesis-figure scripts (report/*_thesis.py, report/*_ch4.py), has a celldform-<name> command (see the CLI reference). The thesis-figure scripts redraw the figures of the thesis text from the saved results and are run by path, for example python scripts/report/plot_cv_thesis.py; they are not installed as commands.

Layout — scripts are grouped by pipeline stage (reorganised 2026-09-17)

scripts/
  data/        organize_dataset · extract_frames · preprocess_frames
  annotation/  annotate · annotate_frame · preview_masks · validate_masks
  training/    train_unet · train_experiment · train_cv_fold · train_deploy_model ·
               train_nnunet_cv · train_student_cv · distill_ensemble
  evaluation/  evaluate_unet · eval_native · eval_nnunet · summarize_cv · compare_postswap · ...
  inference/   infer · predict_single_frame
  hpc/         SLURM jobs for the NSU cluster: training/ and evaluation/ mirror the folders above (see hpc.md)
  report/      build_report_assets and the figure/table generators it drives

Scripts import celldform via Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent, so moving one between folders means fixing that hop. report/render_holdout_comparison.py additionally reaches into annotation/ for preview_masks. Training and evaluation reach across too (split 2026-10-07): evaluation/evaluate_unet.py imports CellDataset from training/train_unet.py, and training/train_nnunet_cv.py imports score from evaluation/eval_nnunet.py.

All scripts live under scripts/<stage>/ and are thin wrappers or standalone tools. Run them directly with python scripts/<stage>/<name>.py, or as the console command celldform-<name> (underscores become dashes): every script outside hpc/ and maintenance/ has one, and celldform lists them all. See CLI Reference.

docs.title: annotation/annotate.py — napari annotation tool
docs.text:
Opens every image in an annotation pool, in order, in napari — including already-annotated ones, so N/B can freely browse and correct earlier work rather than only stepping through what's left. The viewer opens on the first not-yet-annotated image (not the start of the pool); revisiting an annotated frame loads its saved mask instead of a blank one, and the window title shows [saved] for frames that already have a mask on disk. Paint the cell mask on the Labels layer, then press S to save and advance.

python scripts/annotation/annotate.py                             # 01_annotate_pool (default)
python scripts/annotation/annotate.py --pool 02_unet_holdout      # holdout set
python scripts/annotation/annotate.py --multiclass                # experimental 3-class labels (same 40 images)
Option Default Description --pool 01_annotate_pool Pool folder name under data/frames/ --image-dir data/frames/<pool> Override source image directory --mask-dir data/masks/<pool> Override mask output directory --multiclass off Annotate 3 classes (0=background, 1=trapped cell, 2=other/decoy object) instead of binary. Masks default to data/masks/<pool>_multiclass/ and are seeded from the existing binary mask (as label 1) when one exists, so you only need to paint decoy objects

Keybindings:

Key Action 2 Paint brush 3 Eraser [ / ] Smaller / larger brush Ctrl+Z Undo last stroke S Save mask → next image N Skip (no save) → next image B Previous image P Toggle paint mode (napari default — left alone) - / = Step the active paint label down/up (multiclass mode)

P vs. B

P used to mean "previous image" but napari's Labels layer binds it by default to "toggle preserve labels," which shadows any viewer-level binding while the mask layer is active. B is reclaimed for "previous" instead; P is left as napari's default paint-mode toggle.

Binary mode: masks are saved as uint8 PNGs with values 0 (background) / 255 (cell). Multiclass mode: masks are saved with raw label values 0/1/2 (not binarized) — use scripts/annotation/preview_masks.py to view them, since label values 1–2 are visually indistinguishable from background in a plain image viewer.

docs.title: annotation/preview_masks.py — colorized mask preview
docs.text:
Renders saved masks as real color PNGs, mask alone against a black background — no napari needed, and no raw frame loaded or blended in. Multiclass masks (label ids 0/1/2) are nearly invisible in a plain image viewer; this renders background as black, label 1 (trapped cell) as green, and label 2 (other/decoy) as red. Legacy binary masks (0/255) also work — foreground renders green.

python scripts/annotation/preview_masks.py                                    # 01_annotate_pool_multiclass (default)
python scripts/annotation/preview_masks.py --pool 01_annotate_pool            # binary masks
python scripts/annotation/preview_masks.py --limit 10
Option Default Description --pool 01_annotate_pool_multiclass Pool folder name under data/masks/ --mask-dir data/masks/<pool> Override mask directory --output-dir data/masks/<pool>_preview Override output directory --limit none Only preview the first N masks

docs.title: report/build_report_assets.py — rebuild every progress-report figure and table
docs.text:
Single entry point for the progress report's assets. It pins the arguments each figure was generated with and drives the individual plot scripts, so nothing in the report depends on remembering a command line.

python scripts/report/build_report_assets.py                     # build everything
python scripts/report/build_report_assets.py --list              # show job names, run nothing
python scripts/report/build_report_assets.py --dry-run           # print the commands, run nothing
python scripts/report/build_report_assets.py --only sweep pools  # rebuild a subset
python scripts/report/build_report_assets.py --report-root ../masters_thesis

Figures are written to <report-root>/main_work/images/, LaTeX tables to <report-root>/main_work/tables/ (the report \input{}s those). Intermediates from the comparison-strip renderer stay in results/_report_strips/ rather than cluttering the report repo.

Option Default Description --report-root ../masters_thesis Where to write figures and tables --only all Space-separated job names (see --list) --list off Print job names and exit --dry-run off Print each command without running it --compile off Also run pdflatex the required number of times and delete the temp files --tex progress_report_9_10_26.tex Report to compile with --compile 
python scripts/report/build_report_assets.py --compile   # assets, then compile, then clean up

The report must be compiled at least twice

Cross-references and \captionof numbers resolve through the .aux file, and the temp files are deleted after every build — so a single pdflatex pass always starts cold and renders every reference as ?? (e.g. §??). --compile runs the passes needed and then fails loudly if anything is still unresolved, rather than shipping a PDF with ?? in it.

Run it after any change to the frame pools, the masks, or results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl, then recompile the report. Every number in the document comes from one of the scripts it drives, so a stale figure means this wasn't run — not that a number needs editing by hand.

docs.title: report/make_report_tables.py — emit the report's LaTeX tables from the data
docs.text:
Generates .tex fragments the report \input{}s, so the tables can't drift from the pools the way hand-typed ones can.

python scripts/report/make_report_tables.py percell --output ../masters_thesis/main_work/tables/percell.tex
python scripts/report/make_report_tables.py headline --output ../masters_thesis/main_work/tables/headline.tex \
    --run multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_base_cos="No augmentation (noise only)" \
    --run multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos="Scale augmentation" \
    --baseline multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_base_cos \
    --emph multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos

percell counts frames per cell across 01_annotate_pool, 03_mask_factory and 02_unet_holdout and checks each frame for a mask. headline looks each run up in the eval log by (checkpoint, filter) and computes the delta column against --baseline; --extra-run adds an italic row below a rule for runs that are not comparable. Both write a % GENERATED header — edit the script, not the output.

docs.title: report/plot_pool_flow.py — frame-pool provenance diagram
docs.text:
Replaces a pool-summary table: shows which cells go where, that 01_annotate_pool is drawn from 03_mask_factory at different frame indices, and where the evaluation firewall sits. All counts are read off disk.

python scripts/report/plot_pool_flow.py --output results/pool_flow.png

docs.title: report/plot_cell_sizes.py — per-cell trapped-cell size
docs.text:
Measures mean label-1 area per cell from the annotation masks and plots every cell on one axis, with the training range as a band. Makes "the development cells are smaller than the training cells" checkable rather than asserted.

python scripts/report/plot_cell_sizes.py --output results/cell_sizes.png

docs.title: report/plot_split_change.py — train/val split before and after
docs.text:
Two stacked bars showing the training pool growing by reclaiming an unused test split. Counts are arguments, not derived — the old split is historical and not reproducible from disk — and are printed on every run.

python scripts/report/plot_split_change.py --before 293 78 54 --after 371 54 0

docs.title: report/render_holdout_comparison.py — raw/labelled/masks-only/overlay comparison strip
docs.text:
Renders the four-figure holdout comparison used in the thesis progress reports: N evenly-spaced frames from one holdout cell, shown as (1) raw unannotated frames, (2) the multiclass ground-truth annotation (via preview_masks.py's own _colorize(), not a re-drawn approximation), (3) ground truth vs. U-Net prediction on a black background (mask-only), and (4) the same comparison overlaid on the original frame. All four share one auto-computed crop window and panel size, so the cell renders at the same scale in every figure. Every panel carries its own frame index in a label band above the image, so a figure printed in a report can be traced back to the exact files on disk — pass --no-frame-labels for bare panels.

python scripts/report/render_holdout_comparison.py \
    --pool 02_unet_holdout --cell high_cell9 \
    --checkpoint checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf32_reg2_cos/unet_best.pt

python scripts/report/render_holdout_comparison.py \
    --pool 02_unet_holdout --cell low_cell6 \
    --checkpoint checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256/unet_best.pt --base-features 64

unet.base_features/out_channels/in_channels are read from the checkpoint directory's own saved config.yaml when present; pass --base-features etc. to override or when no sibling config exists. The crop auto-sizes to contain the trapped cell, nearby decoy objects (within --decoy-radius, default 150px — excludes far-flung debris elsewhere in the frame), and the largest predicted region across the selected frames, padded by --pad (default 45px); pass --half-width/--half-height to pin it explicitly instead. --gt-color/--pred-color/--overlap-color take R,G,B and only affect figures (3)/(4) — the ground-truth-annotation figure (2) always uses preview_masks.py's own green/red convention.

Option Default Description --pool 02_unet_holdout Pool folder under data/frames/ and data/preprocessed/evaluate/ --cell (required) Cell filename prefix, e.g. high_cell9 --checkpoint (required) Path to a trained .pt checkpoint --n-frames 5 Evenly-spaced frames to render --frame-indices none Comma-separated 6-digit indices instead of auto-selecting --half-width / --half-height auto Pin the crop size instead of computing it --pad 45 Padding (px) around the auto-computed crop --decoy-radius 150 Max distance (px) from the trapped cell for a decoy to count toward the auto-crop --alpha 0.55 Overlay blend strength for figure (4) --no-frame-labels off Render bare panels, with no frame-index band above each one --label-color / --label-bg 255,255,255 / 20,20,20 R,G,B for the frame-index text and its band --output-dir results/holdout_comparisons/<pool>_<cell> Output directory

docs.title: annotation/validate_masks.py — mask validation gate
docs.text:
Validates the masks that are present in a pool, and (by default) that every frame in the pool has one. Use as a pre-training gate.

python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py                          # 01_annotate_pool
python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py --pool 02_unet_holdout
python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py --multiclass              # validates 01_annotate_pool_multiclass
python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py --no-completeness         # skip the "every frame has a mask" check
Option Default Description --pool 01_annotate_pool Pool folder name (used for both data/frames/<pool> and data/masks/<pool>) --mask-dir data/masks/<pool> (or <pool>_multiclass with --multiclass) Override mask directory --image-dir data/frames/<pool> Override frame directory (completeness check) --no-completeness off Skip the "every pool image has a mask" check entirely --multiclass off Validate 3-class masks (0/1/2) instead of binary (0/255)

Checks performed:

Check Fail condition (binary) Fail condition (--multiclass) Present Frame in the pool has no corresponding mask file (skippable with --no-completeness) same Readable File cannot be decoded by OpenCV same Binary/label-valid Pixel values other than 0 or 255 Pixel values other than 0, 1, or 2 Non-empty No foreground pixels (255) at all No foreground pixels of any class (neither label 1 nor label 2) — a mask with only a decoy object (label 2) and no trapped cell is a valid deliberate negative and passes

Exits with code 0 if all checks pass, 1 if any issues are found. Reports Valid: N/N (100%) against the full pool count (or the mask count with --no-completeness).

docs.title: data/preprocess_frames.py — manual preprocessing
docs.text:
Applies PreprocessingPipeline to frames and saves PNGs (256×256 by default). Required before training. Optionally resizes masks to match.

Mask-gated processing

When --masks is passed, only frames that have a corresponding mask in data/masks/<pool>/ are processed. Frames without a mask are skipped. The summary line reports how many were skipped.

python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks                        # train pool
python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks --pool 02_unet_holdout # evaluate pool
python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --pool 03_mask_factory          # inference pool
python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks --compare --n-compare 10
python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks --target-size 128 128   # override output resolution
Option Default Description --pool 01_annotate_pool Pool folder name --stage auto-detected train, evaluate, or inference --masks off Also resize and save masks (binary or label, nearest-neighbour) --compare off Save pipeline stage comparison figures --n-compare 5 Number of images to generate figures for --image-dir data/frames/<pool> Override source directory --output-dir data/preprocessed/<stage>/<pool>/inputs Override frame output --mask-dir data/masks/<pool> Override source mask directory --mask-output-dir data/preprocessed/<stage>/<pool>/labels Override mask output --target-size 256 256 Output spatial size H W. Both dims should stay divisible by 16 (U-Net's 4 downsampling steps) — the U-Net is fully convolutional, so no model code changes are needed, but whatever size is chosen here is what CellDataset will load during training

Stage auto-detection:

Pool Stage 01_annotate_pool train 02_unet_holdout evaluate 03_mask_factory inference

docs.title: training/train_unet.py — U-Net training
docs.text:
Trains the U-Net on preprocessed data. Expects already-preprocessed PNGs at whatever size was used for preprocessing (256×256 by default) — no preprocessing is applied internally. Reads unet.out_channels from the config: 1 (default) trains binary segmentation; >1 trains multiclass (CellDataset loads raw integer label masks instead of binarising, and _DiceCELoss replaces _DiceBCELoss).

python scripts/training/train_unet.py --config configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml   # frozen scheme
python scripts/training/train_unet.py --config configs/default.yaml --seed 123
python scripts/training/train_unet.py --config configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml --tag auto
python scripts/training/train_unet.py --config configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml --domain-oversample-weight 8.0
Option Default Description --config configs/default.yaml YAML config file --seed config value Random seed override --domain-oversample-weight config value (1.0 if unset) Sampling weight for domain_-prefixed (real-cell) train frames vs. legacy frames — builds a WeightedRandomSampler. 1.0 = off/uniform; pass 1.0 explicitly to force it off even if the config enables it. See Training Results — Domain Gap (tested at weight=8.0: no improvement on the small real-cell test sample available so far). --tag none Suffix appended to the saved training-curve filename (e.g. --tag auto → unet_training_curves_v6_auto.png), for distinguishing runs at a glance

The script reads data.frames_dir and data.masks_dir from the config. Pairs frames and masks by filename stem. Saves best and last checkpoints to checkpoint_dir. After training, it reloads unet_best.pt (not necessarily the last epoch's weights, which can be past the peak validation DSC on small datasets) before running final evaluation and plotting the training curves.

docs.title: evaluation/evaluate_unet.py — holdout evaluation
docs.text:
Evaluates a trained U-Net on 02_unet_holdout and reports the thesis-reportable segmentation metrics.

python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py --checkpoint checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256/unet_best.pt \
    --config configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml   # frozen scheme — --config must match out_channels
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py --checkpoint checkpoints/unet_best.pt --pool 02_unet_holdout  # binary baseline
Option Default Description --checkpoint required Path to trained .pt checkpoint --pool 02_unet_holdout Pool to evaluate --config configs/default.yaml YAML config --batch-size 8 Inference batch size --results-log results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl JSONL file each run's metrics get appended to --no-save-results off Skip the append (stdout only)

Metrics reported: DSC, IoU, precision, recall, accuracy. When the checkpoint's config has unet.out_channels > 1, results are reported per class (background, trapped_cell, ...) instead of as a single flat table.

Every run is also logged to disk (unless --no-save-results) as one JSON line appended to results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl — full-precision metrics per class, plus timestamp/checkpoint/config/pool/n_images/multiclass. Printing to stdout alone doesn't survive the terminal scrolling past it; this is the durable record to check a reported number against, or to re-derive a summary table from later (json.loads each line).

docs.title: data/organize_dataset.py — dataset organiser
docs.text:
Thin wrapper around celldform.acquisition.organiser.organise().

python scripts/data/organize_dataset.py
python scripts/data/organize_dataset.py --every-n 100 --domain-adapt-n 10
python scripts/data/organize_dataset.py --no-clean --domain-adapt-n 20   # expand domain-adapt only, don't wipe data/frames/ — run 2026-08-19

Equivalent to celldform-organize-dataset. See CLI Reference. The domain_adapt cell list in celldform/acquisition/organiser.py covers all 11 03_mask_factory cells (as of 2026-08-10, extended from 4); --domain-adapt-n was raised 5→20/cell on 2026-08-19 — see Training Results — Domain Gap for why. Re-running with a larger N doesn't lose frames/masks from an earlier N — every domain_* file already on disk is kept and re-enumerated into the manifest, and legacy frames reserved in 02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout/ are always excluded from the copy regardless of N (a contamination bug where this wasn't true was found and fixed the same day).

docs.title: data/extract_frames.py — single video extraction
docs.text:
Thin wrapper around FrameExtractor for a single video.

python scripts/data/extract_frames.py --video data/raw/high/"cell 1 high 50 increments.mp4"

Equivalent to celldform-extract-frames. See CLI Reference.

docs.title: inference/infer.py — full inference pipeline
docs.text:
Runs stages 1–6 on a video or directory of preprocessed images.

python scripts/inference/infer.py \
    --video data/raw/high/"cell 1 high 50 increments.mp4" \
    --unet-ckpt checkpoints/unet_best.pt \
    --classifier-ckpt checkpoints/svm.pkl

Equivalent to celldform-infer. See CLI Reference.

docs.title: evaluation/compare_postswap.py — enforce the noise floor on comparisons
docs.text:
Reads results/postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline/eval_log.jsonl and compares runs against the series baseline, per development cell and over all cells together.

python scripts/evaluation/compare_postswap.py                      # every run vs. baseline
python scripts/evaluation/compare_postswap.py --runs A B           # just these
python scripts/evaluation/compare_postswap.py --seeds A B C        # aggregate seeds: mean ± sd

It exists to stop a number that looks exciting being recorded as a finding. Measured seed-only spread on this pipeline is evaluated sd 0.057, so a difference between two single runs has SE ≈ 0.081 and needs roughly twice that to be believable. Anything below 0.161 prints as INCONCLUSIVE:

  => INCONCLUSIVE. Evaluated delta +0.048 is inside the +/-0.161 noise floor.
     Log as screened, not as a result. Three seeds on BOTH arms to decide it.

This is not a formality

Two results in this project were recorded as findings and later retracted for exactly this reason — the scale-augmentation recipe (+0.066) and Focal–Tversky (+0.023, whose seed repeat came back −0.049). Both are smaller than the noise.

docs.title: training/train_experiment.py — train + evaluate one run, filed correctly
docs.text:
python scripts/training/train_experiment.py postswap/experiment_1b_loss e1b_lovasz_s42
python scripts/training/train_experiment.py postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline postswap_ftl_cw142_s46 --seed 46

Expects configs/<experiment>/<run>.yaml whose checkpoint_dir is checkpoints/<experiment>/<run>. Trains (log in logs/<experiment>/<run>.log, curves in results/<experiment>/), then scores the checkpoint on the testing set per cell and pooled at the config's own size (evaluation/eval_testing_set.py → results/<experiment>/eval_log.jsonl) and at native resolution (evaluation/eval_native.py → eval_log_native.jsonl). Extra arguments go to train_unet.py. Compare runs afterwards with compare_postswap.py. This replaces the old run_postswap.sh (= train_experiment.py postswap/experiment_0a_seed_baseline <run>).

Use it rather than calling train_unet.py directly, so artefacts land in the right folders and the comparison happens automatically.

docs.title: notebooks/pipeline_walkthrough.ipynb — the pipeline end to end
docs.text:
A runnable tour of all seven stages against the data actually on disk: pool inspection and the firewall check, frame extraction, mask validation, preprocessing, the train/val split, evaluation with the noise floor applied, features, classification, biomechanics and inference.

jupyter lab notebooks/pipeline_walkthrough.ipynb

Most cells only read and display. The four that write are each gated:

RUN_ORGANISE = False      # rebuilds data/frames/ from raw  ← destructive
RUN_PREPROCESS = False    # rewrites data/preprocessed/**
RUN_TRAINING = False      # ~15 min on an 8 GB GPU
RUN_EVAL = False          # runs the model over the development set

They print what they would do while the flag is False.

docs.title: Notebook outputs are stripped automatically
docs.text:
nbstripout is installed as a git clean filter, so outputs and execution_count never reach a commit — the working file keeps them, git stores only the source. Without it a single re-run produces a multi-megabyte diff of base64 PNGs in which nothing meaningful changed.

.gitattributes is committed, but the filter command lives in .git/config, which is not. After cloning, run it once:

pip install -e ".[dev]"
nbstripout --install --attributes .gitattributes
git config --local --get filter.nbstripout.clean    # should print a command

If you skip this, git silently does nothing — an undefined filter is not an error — and outputs go into history as normal.

docs.title: The notebook sandbox
docs.text:
Runs launched from the notebook write to configs/notebook/, checkpoints/notebook/, logs/notebook/ and results/notebook/, never into preswap/ or postswap/. That keeps exploratory output out of the experimental record that compare_postswap.py and the report tables are generated from. All four are gitignored.

promote() moves a sandbox run up into configs/postswap/ when it turns out to matter. It verifies the run against the config snapshot saved inside its checkpoint directory — so a run whose config was edited afterwards is refused rather than silently promoted.

Appendix

The last section lists the traps this pipeline has actually fallen into — stale preprocessing silently breaking the firewall, single-run deltas below the noise floor, an oversized validation group voiding a run. Worth reading before a first experiment.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text: November 2026. What exists, what has been measured, and what has not. Earlier work is kept in the research log.

docs.title: What the project delivers
docs.text: Part State Segmentation of the trapped cell: a U-Net (384 px native crop) and an nnU-Net benchmark trained and tested at the level of whole cells Feature extraction with five per-frame quality checks (a frame that fails is not used) working HER2 classifier: step-level and cell-level logistic regression, averaged validated by leave-one-cell-out on 15 cells Desktop app that analyzes a recorded video and reports the HER2 class with its evidence working; ships no models, see the app Real-time operation, connection to the instrument's control software not done: the app analyses recordings (see below)

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Every number below holds out whole cells: frames of one cell are never in both training and test, because frames of the same cell are almost identical. 15 cells (9 high HER2, 6 low HER2), one cell line (SKBR3), one setup.

Segmentation: Dice score of the trapped cell, mean over cells ± standard deviation

Model Test protocol Mean over cells High HER2 Low HER2 Worst cell U-Net, 384 px crop 5 rounds, random cells held out 0.855 ± 0.114 0.802 0.934 0.625 U-Net, 384 px crop leave-one-cell-out, 15 rounds 0.865 ± 0.092 0.834 0.910 0.710 nnU-Net (2D) leave-one-cell-out, 15 rounds 0.940 ± 0.069 0.919 0.972 0.725

High-HER2 cells are harder to segment than low-HER2 cells. The U-Net takes about 40 ms per frame on a modern GPU, the nnU-Net about 0.4–0.5 s. A cell-level result varies a lot between cells, so a difference of a few hundredths between two single runs is not evidence of anything (see the research log for how large the noise is).

Classification: HER2 class of a cell

Using masks from the nnU-Net, the classifier called 14 of 15 cells correctly in leave-one-cell-out testing (AUC 0.94, permutation p ≈ 0.002). It was then fitted on all 15 cells; that final model is what the app uses.

docs.title: Limits you should know about
docs.text:
• One setup, 15 cells. The result says how well the method works on cells recorded the way these were (a laser ramp from 500 to 1200 mA in 50 mA steps, 30 s per level). It does not show that it transfers to other instruments, cell lines or protocols.
  • A recording from a different setup may not work. On four recordings from a newer setup (colour camera, a 298–1000 mA ramp in steps of about 9 s) the U-Net found the cell in only 2–13 % of the measured frames, so the app correctly gave no verdict. Using it there needs new annotated frames and fine-tuning.
  • The app is cautious on purpose. It gives a verdict only when at least 3 laser steps are usable and 80 % of the measured frames pass the checks. The classifier was validated on whole recordings (10 or more steps), so a recording of 3 to 9 steps gets a result labelled short recording from the step model alone, which is weaker. An optional provisional verdict exists for recordings that fail the checks; it is always labelled not validated and is not a result.
  • Not real-time. The U-Net is faster than the camera's 45.5 ms frame interval, but the delivered software analyses recordings and is not connected to the instrument.
  • Research software. It is not a medical device and not for clinical decisions.

docs.title: What would come next
docs.text: More cells and a second setup for external validation; fine-tuning for the newer recording protocol; and, if wanted, a version that runs alongside the instrument.

docs.title: U-Net Training Results
docs.text:
Superseded — read this first (2026-09-17)

Later results (random whole-cell cross-validation, a 384 px native crop, nnU-Net, the classifier and the desktop app) are on the Project status page; this page is the earlier tuning record.

Every tuning delta on this page is smaller than the measured noise.

Re-running one configuration changing only the random seed moved the evaluated DSC from 0.691 to 0.619 — a swing of 0.072. A three-seed repeat with the train/val split pinned gave sd 0.057, range 0.111 on the complete 203-frame development set (0.047 / 0.093 on the 172-frame partial set).

Quantity Magnitude Seed-only swing 0.072–0.111 Focal–Tversky "gain" 0.023 — swamped Scale augmentation (the settled recipe) 0.066 — inside the band Regularisation sweep deltas 0.005–0.02 — far inside

None of the single-run comparisons below are established. They are kept as the record of what was tried, not as evidence of what works. A single run resolves differences above roughly 0.16; report multi-seed means with spread instead.

Also note the development set changed on 17 September (high-10 into training, high-1 into evaluation), so pre- and post-swap numbers are not comparable at all.

Current baseline: postswap_ftl_cw142_s42, evaluated DSC 0.816 ± 0.057 (3-seed mean, 4 cells, 203 frames). See configs/README.md; the checkpoints themselves are not in the repository.

Training results from the first 39-mask smoke test through the current best checkpoint. Runs 1-4 below (2026-07/08) established the label scheme (multiclass, 256×256, frozen 2026-08-10) and surfaced a real legacy/real-cell domain gap. If you only read one section, read The 2026-09 full evaluation sweep — it's the most consequential finding in this document: an internal-validation-optimized checkpoint that looked excellent turned out to generalize roughly 2.6× worse than a "worse-looking" one, once evaluated against genuinely novel cells for the first time.

Current state (2026-09-10): 02_unet_holdout's development set (high_cell9 + low_cell6) is fully annotated and has been evaluated against every checkpoint.
