Best real-generalization checkpoint: checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt, evaluated DSC 0.671 — scale augmentation alone, under the cosine schedule and 90% training split. A third cell, high_cell10, is reserved as a blind test and deliberately not yet annotated — see Next Steps.

The bf64_allaug result (0.572) was retracted on 2026-09-10

That run was reported as "+0.047 from combining all augmentations," but it had also switched to a cosine schedule and folded the unused test split into training (293 → 371 frames). A controlled re-run with those two changes held fixed and no augmentation scores 0.605 — above the combined recipe. The gain was the schedule and the extra data. Under a matched config, scale augmentation alone reaches 0.671 and combined augmentation lands at 0.572, below doing nothing. See The controlled augmentation re-run below.

docs.title: Run 1 — Baseline (no class imbalance correction)
docs.text:
Masks: 39 annotated | Epochs: 50 | Loss: Dice+BCE (α=0.5, no pos_weight)

Metric Value DSC 0.0902 IoU 0.0473 Precision 0.0511 Recall 0.3880 Accuracy 0.9857

Diagnosis: The model learned to predict mostly background. SKBR3 cells occupy roughly 0.18% of each 256×256 frame (~118 pixels out of 65,536), giving a ~550:1 background-to-cell pixel ratio. Without compensation, the BCE loss is dominated by background pixels — achieving near-zero loss simply by ignoring the cell. High accuracy (0.985) is misleading here: it reflects correct background prediction, not cell segmentation. Low precision (0.05) combined with moderate recall (0.39) indicates the model was guessing large regions that partially overlapped the cell.

docs.title: Run 2 — With class imbalance correction
docs.text:
Masks: 30 annotated out of 220 available (13.6%) | Epochs: 50 | Loss: Dice+BCE (α=0.3, pos_weight=100)

DSC 0.72 from just 30 of 220 masks

This result was produced using only 30 hand-drawn masks — 13.6% of the 220-image annotation pool (the pool was briefly misdocumented as 240 elsewhere; see CLAUDE.md — it's 220, 200 legacy + 20 domain-adapt). The remaining 190 frames were not yet annotated at this point. A DSC of 0.72 at this stage was a strong indicator that the annotations were correct and the pipeline was working as expected. The full pool has since been annotated — see Run 4 below.

Metric Value DSC 0.7162 IoU 0.5581 Precision 0.5594 Recall 0.9958 Accuracy 0.9986

Interpretation: Adding pos_weight=100 to the BCE term makes each cell pixel count as 100 background pixels in the loss, forcing the model to prioritise finding the cell. The result is near-perfect recall (the model finds virtually all cell pixels) at the cost of slightly over-segmenting the boundary (precision=0.56). This is the expected trade-off at this sample size — a model that over-segments slightly is preferable to one that misses cells. DSC of 0.72 with only 30 training samples confirms that annotations are correct and consistent.

The loss_alpha=0.3 change (from 0.5) gives Dice loss 70% of the total signal, further counteracting the imbalance.

docs.title: Training curves (Run 2)
docs.text:
Left — Segmentation loss: Both train and val loss decrease steadily across 50 epochs, converging to ~0.80. Val loss tracks train loss closely, indicating no significant overfitting with this sample size.

Right — Validation DSC: DSC stays near zero for the first ~20 epochs while the model learns basic image features, then climbs sharply between epochs 20–30 as it begins detecting the cell shape. DSC reaches ~0.72 by epoch 50. The oscillation in the second half is expected — the validation set is only ~5 images, so a single mis-segmented frame has a large effect on the reported score.

docs.title: Run 3 — Binary vs. multiclass label scheme × resolution ablation
docs.text:
Same 40 annotated frames as Run 2 (up from 30), used to isolate two variables against the binary 256×256 baseline: the annotation label scheme (binary vs. 3-class) and the preprocessed input resolution (128×128 vs. 256×256). Four configs, each holding the other three variables fixed (seed 42, 100 epochs, loss_alpha=0.3):

Config Labels Resolution Loss weighting Trapped-cell DSC Best epoch configs/binary_experiment_128.yaml binary 128×128 pos_weight=50 0.590 92 configs/multiclass_experiment.yaml 3-class 128×128 class_weights=[1,3,3] 0.736 99 configs/binary_experiment_256.yaml binary 256×256 pos_weight=50 0.763 99 configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml 3-class 256×256 class_weights=[1,3,3] 0.784 73

Training curves and per-class metric tables: results/unet_training_curves_v13_binary_128.png through v16_multi_256.png.

Multiclass detail (256×256, configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml):

Class DSC IoU Precision Recall Accuracy background 0.996 0.993 1.000 0.993 0.993 trapped_cell 0.784 0.645 0.757 0.813 0.999 other/decoy 0.682 0.518 0.518 0.999 0.994 mean 0.821 0.719 0.758 0.935 0.995

Interpretation:

  • Labeling scheme matters more than resolution alone. At 128×128, adding the decoy-object class raised trapped-cell DSC from 0.590 to 0.736 (+0.146) — a larger jump than switching binary from 128×128 to 256×256 (0.590 → 0.763, +0.173, comparable magnitude) or multiclass from 128×128 to 256×256 (0.736 → 0.784, +0.048, smaller). The best result combines both: multiclass at 256×256.
  • Why multiclass helps: giving decoy objects (untrapped cells, debris, lookalike blobs) their own class instead of leaving them as unlabeled background stops the loss from penalizing the model for segmenting them — under the binary scheme, a decoy that visually resembles the trapped cell is background the model is punished for finding, which pushes precision down indiscriminately. Explicitly modeling it as its own class lets the network learn to distinguish "cell-like blob, but not the trapped one" from "the trapped cell," rather than lumping both into one binary decision.
  • The decoy class itself is harder (DSC 0.682 vs. 0.784 for trapped_cell) — expected, since decoy objects are a heterogeneous category (any non-trapped cell-like blob) rather than the single consistent target the trapped-cell class represents.
  • Multiclass converges faster and can overfit sooner: the 256×256 multiclass run peaked at epoch 73 (val DSC 0.784) then declined to ~0.69 by epoch 100, while the binary run kept improving to epoch 99. scripts/training/train_unet.py reloads unet_best.pt before final evaluation specifically to guard against this — final metrics reflect the peak, not wherever the fixed 100-epoch budget happened to end.
  • Caveat: these are 40-mask, single-seed runs — not yet a controlled statistical comparison.

Decision (2026-08-10): multiclass @ 256×256 is the frozen label scheme and resolution going forward. binary_experiment_{128,256}.yaml and the 128×128 multiclass config are no longer being actively pursued — kept only as this historical ablation record. This does not change the downstream contract: UNet.predict(..., binary_output=True) collapses the 3-class map to trapped-cell-only binary before MorphologyExtractor and everything past it (commit b6e181b) — multiclass is a training-time-only mechanism for a sharper trapped-cell boundary.

docs.title: Run 4 — Full 220-mask pool
docs.text:
Masks: 220 annotated out of 220 available (100% — annotation pool complete) | Epochs: 100 (best: 45) | Same hyperparameters as Run 3's multiclass_experiment_256.yaml

Class DSC IoU Precision Recall background 0.999 0.999 1.000 0.999 trapped_cell 0.943 0.891 0.912 0.974 other/decoy 0.759 0.612 0.697 0.834

Training curves: results/unet_training_curves_v19.png. The group-aware split (leave-one-cell-out, confirmed in scripts/training/train_unet.py's _build_groups/_group_split) means this jump from 0.784 (Run 3, 40 masks) is real added-data signal, not leakage — but see the caveat immediately below before treating 0.943 as the thesis number.

docs.title: Domain Gap
docs.text:
The 0.943 DSC above is measured on a validation split that is 100% legacy-domain (2021 microscope) frames — reproducing the group-aware split with seed 42 shows 0 of the 35 validation frames are domain_-prefixed (real trapped-cell) frames. Breaking the held-out test split out by source tells the real story:

Test subset (unseen in training) n Trapped-cell DSC Recall Legacy (2021) 18 0.944 (matches the reported 0.943) 0.972 Domain-adapt (real trapped cell) 5 0.538 0.386

High precision (0.895) with collapsed recall means the model under-segments real cells rather than hallucinating — it hasn't learned the live-imaging appearance well. Root cause: only 20/220 (9%) of training frames were real-domain, drawn from just 4 of the 11 usable 03_mask_factory cells, so real frames were outnumbered ~10:1 by legacy frames in the actual train split (15 vs. 147). n=5 is small enough not to be precise, but the direction is unambiguous — 0.943 should not be treated as the real-world number until it's confirmed on the full 02_unet_holdout set (101 real-cell frames).

docs.title: Mitigations tried
docs.text:
1. More real cells in training (run 2026-08-19). celldform/acquisition/organiser.py's domain_adapt video list was extended from 4 cells to all 11 03_mask_factory cells, and --domain-adapt-n was raised 5→20/cell (celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean --domain-adapt-n 20) rather than waiting on the honest 02_unet_holdout DSC to pick a value — the decision was made to grow the pool first and use the legacy-vs-domain DSC breakdown on the internal train/val/test split as the interim feedback signal instead, keeping 02_unet_holdout reserved for the eventual thesis number (see Next Steps). 01_annotate_pool grew from 220 → 428 images (200 legacy + 228 domain-adapt); 208 of the domain frames are new and pending annotation. Frames can safely belong to both 01_annotate_pool (segmentation training) and 03_mask_factory (classifier feature extraction) — same precedent as the existing 4 domain-adapt cells, no contamination, since _domain_adapt() and _extract_group() sample different frame indices from the same video.

2. Oversampling existing domain frames (tried, did not help). Added training.domain_oversample_weight (celldform/config.py, default 1.0) — a WeightedRandomSampler (scripts/training/train_unet.py) that resamples domain_-prefixed train frames more often per epoch, at zero new-annotation cost. Toggle via a config's training: block or the --domain-oversample-weight <N> CLI flag on celldform-train-unet/scripts/training/train_unet.py. A/B tested at weight=8.0 (configs/multiclass_experiment_256_domain_oversample.yaml, ~12%→~41% real-domain frames/epoch) against the Run 4 baseline:

Test subset (n) Baseline (weight=1) Oversampled (weight=8) Legacy (18) DSC 0.944 DSC 0.946 (unchanged) Domain-adapt (5) DSC 0.538, recall 0.386 DSC 0.455, recall 0.30 (worse)

No improvement — resampling only exposes the model to the same 15 unique real images more often; it can't manufacture appearance diversity that isn't there, and likely overfits harder to the 3 real cells already seen (precision rose to 0.947 while recall fell further). Conclusion: mitigation 1 (more real cells) is necessary — resampling existing frames is not a substitute.

docs.title: Checkpoint-loading bug found and fixed (2026-08-10)
docs.text: UNet.from_checkpoint() (celldform/segmentation/unet.py) did a bare load_state_dict(torch.load(path)), but SegmentationTrainer._save_checkpoint() actually wraps weights in {"epoch", "val_dsc", "model_state_dict", ...} — so celldform-infer and scripts/inference/infer.py would crash on any checkpoint training actually produces. evaluate_unet.py and predict_single_frame.py had each independently worked around it with a manual unwrap; tests/test_segmentation.py didn't catch it because it saves a bare state dict via model.save(), never exercising the wrapped-dict path a real training run produces. Fixed to unwrap model_state_dict when present.

docs.title: Contamination bug found and fixed (2026-08-19)
docs.text: organise()'s legacy-image copy step (celldform/acquisition/organiser.py) had no exclusion for the 20 frames permanently reserved into 02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout/ — running celldform-organize-dataset --no-clean to grow the domain-adapt pool (mitigation 1, above) silently recopied all 220 legacy JPGs, holdout included, back into 01_annotate_pool. Caught before annotation touched them (no masks existed yet for those 20 filenames), so no holdout contamination actually reached the model — but a routine --no-clean rerun would eventually have annotated them by accident, since their timestamp-numeric filenames sort before domain_* and scripts/annotation/annotate.py resumes on the first unannotated image. Fixed: organise() now reads whatever's in legacy_holdout/ and permanently excludes those filenames from the legacy copy, so this can't recur on future reruns; the 20 duplicated files were removed from the pool.

docs.title: Domain gap closed (2026-08-27)
docs.text:
The 208 pending domain frames got annotated to completion, bringing 01_annotate_pool to 425 masks (three cell-free frames caught by validate_masks.py's "no trapped-cell pixel" check were removed rather than annotated). Retraining multiclass_experiment_256.yaml on the full pool: domain-adapt test DSC 0.910, recall 0.939 — up from 0.538/0.386 — closing the gap that motivated the whole expansion.

This result is not currently reproducible. A same-config, same-seed rerun landed on a different result days later purely from re-running — root cause was torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True (SegmentationTrainer.__init__, since fixed as a configurable training.cudnn_benchmark knob, default false in the active config), which re-times conv kernels against runtime hardware state each run and isn't suppressed by torch.manual_seed alone. Chasing this down overwrote the epoch-69 checkpoint behind the 0.910 finding twice before the cause was identified, and it was never backed up. Treat 0.910/0.939 as a historical record, not a current number — no checkpoint on disk reproduces it, and it predates the far more important finding below anyway (it was itself measured on the internal validation split, which turned out to be a poor proxy for real generalization regardless of the reproducibility issue).

docs.title: The 2026-09 full evaluation sweep
docs.text: 02_unet_holdout was finally annotated (high_cell9 50 frames + low_cell6 51 frames = 101 frames — the genuine, never-trained-on development set; see Data Layout for why that term, not "test set," is the accurate one) and evaluated against every checkpoint from the ongoing hyperparameter sweep. The result overturned the sweep's own internal conclusions.

docs.title: Internal validation was measuring the wrong thing
docs.text:
The checkpoint that looked best on the internal validation split (bf32_reg2_cos: base_features=32, dropout=0.4, cutout=0.3, cosine schedule — internal val DSC 0.862) scored only DSC 0.163 on high_cell9, the first genuinely novel cell ever evaluated. The checkpoint informally labeled "overfitting" (the original, unregularized base_features=64 run, flagged for a large internal train/val gap) scored 0.428 — roughly 2.6× better on real generalization, despite scoring worse on the very metric the whole sweep had been optimizing against.

Why: the internal validation split draws its "unseen" frames from cell identities the model has trained on (other frames of the same cells) — it measures frame-level generalization within known identities, not generalization to a genuinely new cell. Every hyperparameter decision made against it (dropout level, cutout, weight decay, scheduler, split ratio) had been tuned against the wrong signal.

docs.title: Full 14-checkpoint sweep, evaluated against the real development set
docs.text:
Every checkpoint from the base_features/dropout/cutout/regularization sweep was re-evaluated against the full 101-frame development set (scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py --pool 02_unet_holdout, results logged to results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl):

Checkpoint base_features Recipe Trapped-cell DSC multiclass_experiment_256 64 none (the "overfitting" original) 0.525 bf32_reg 32 dropout 0.3, cutout 0.441 bf32_reg2_wd 32 dropout 0.4, cutout, weight decay 1e-3 0.430 bf32_reg2_det 32 dropout 0.4, cutout, cudnn_benchmark=false 0.422 bf32_reg2 32 dropout 0.4, cutout 0.421 bf32_reg2_swa 32 dropout 0.4, cutout + SWA 0.421 bf32_reg2_wd2 32 dropout 0.4, cutout, cosine, weight decay 1e-3 0.420 bf32_reg2_cos 32 dropout 0.4, cutout, cosine (the internal-val champion) 0.408 bf32 32 none 0.403 bf32_reg3 32 dropout 0.5, cutout 0.400 bf32_reg2_ablate 32 dropout 0.4, cutout, noise/class-weights off 0.388 bf64_reg 64 dropout 0.4, cutout, cosine (reg. recipe at width 64) 0.378 bf32_reg2_split 32 dropout 0.4, cutout, val/test 20%/15% 0.376 domain_oversample 64 domain_oversample_weight=8 (older/smaller pool) 0.229

Every single regularization lever tried — at either width — underperforms the plain, unregularized original on real, never-seen cells. The internal-val overfitting signal was real; fixing it made real-world generalization worse, every time.

Root cause of the gap: high_cell9's and low_cell6's true trapped-cell size (704 / 886 px²) falls at or below every one of the 11 training cells' (825-1549 px²) — a real train/development-set size mismatch, checked and confirmed not to be a laser-power-sampling artifact (training and holdout frames were verified to sample laser power near-identically). The model likely leans on an implicit learned "typical size" from training that doesn't transfer to a genuinely smaller novel cell — visible directly in the metrics as a precision problem, not a recall one: recall sits at 0.6-0.7 almost everywhere in the table above, while precision is the actual discriminator (0.454 for the unregularized original vs. 0.26-0.33 for every regularized variant). The model finds the cell fine; it predicts too much area around it, and regularization consistently made that worse.

Superseded figure (23 September 2026)

The 1549 px² upper bound above is high_cell1 as annotated at the time. That cell was re-annotated on 23 September and now measures 678 px² — the smallest cell in the study, not the largest. The old masks no longer exist. The size mismatch described here was real but smaller than stated, and part of the gap was an annotation artifact. Current ranges: training 688–1449 px², development set 678–1033 px², interleaved. See docs/status.md.

A largest-connected-component post-processing fix was tried and ruled out (made every checkpoint's DSC worse — the false theory was that oversized predictions were one correct blob plus small spurious fragments; the real finding was that 11% of frames get a completely empty raw prediction, and a min_area_px floor discards those small-but-correct low-power predictions while leaving the actual oversized high-power blobs untouched either way). The fix had to happen at the model/training level.

docs.title: Augmentation experiments
docs.text:
Three tried, in order, each testing one new lever against the same unregularized base_features=64 baseline:

1. Brightness/contrast jitter (bf64_bc) — no effect. Random global brightness shift (±0.15) and contrast scale (0.8-1.2×) on the train frame — hypothesis was that CLAHE's local contrast normalization doesn't erase the global exposure level a frame was captured at, which plausibly tracks laser power. Result: DSC 0.501 vs. 0.525 baseline (within noise), and — the more telling number — precision barely moved (0.447 vs. 0.454), the specific thing this was meant to fix. Global intensity jitter doesn't address the over-segmentation; the extra predicted area is more likely a spatial artifact (a halo/glare shape near the cell) than a pure intensity-level effect.

2. Scale/zoom augmentation (bf64_scale) — helped one cell, hurt the other. Random resize (0.7-1.3×) of frame+mask together, then center-crop/pad back to 256×256 — directly targets the size-mismatch finding above. Evaluated DSC improved (0.525 → 0.541) but the per-cell breakdown told a different story:

Original Scale augmentation high_cell9 DSC 0.428 0.368 (worse) high_cell9 precision 0.319 0.259 low_cell6 DSC 0.650 0.719 (better) low_cell6 recall 0.600 0.935

Visual inspection (scripts/report/render_holdout_comparison.py, mask-only GT-vs-prediction comparison) explained the split: low_cell6's original problem was under-detection (the model was missing most of the cell in several frames) — scale augmentation fixed this directly, by teaching the model to accept a more modest-sized blob as valid. high_cell9's problem is over-detection — a spatial artifact the model includes as if it were the cell — a structurally different bug that size tolerance doesn't touch, and arguably slightly worsens by making the model more permissive everywhere. Lesson: always check the per-cell breakdown before calling an all-cells change a win — the evaluated number alone hid a real regression here, and will again with only two development cells.

3. Combined recipe (bf64_allaug) — current best, genuinely improves both cells. All four CellDataset augmentation knobs at once (noise 0.02, cutout 0.3, brightness/contrast 0.5, scale 0.5), cosine scheduler, dropout left off (it's model regularization, not augmentation, and was already shown to hurt), and the internal validation split repurposed from the old, entirely unused test_split (see Data Layout) — 90% of the pool goes to training instead of 69%.

Original Scale only Combined recipe high_cell9 DSC 0.428 0.368 0.482 high_cell9 precision 0.319 0.259 0.365 low_cell6 DSC 0.650 0.719 0.693 low_cell6 precision 0.708 0.584 0.837 Evaluated DSC 0.525 0.541 0.572

checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt is the current best on the development set — the first checkpoint all sweep to improve both cells over the original baseline rather than trading one for the other. Not yet understood: why the combination lifts high_cell9's precision specifically when scale_prob alone didn't (worth an ablation — e.g. drop brightness_contrast_prob, which showed nothing alone, and check whether the win holds without it).

docs.title: The controlled augmentation re-run
docs.text:
2026-09-10. The most important correction in this document — read it before trusting any augmentation result above.

The bf64_allaug run was reported as "+0.047 from combining all four augmentation knobs." It changed three independent things at once, only one of which was augmentation:

  1. all four augmentation knobs on (cutout_prob 0→0.3, brightness_contrast_prob 0→0.5, scale_prob kept at 0.5),
  2. training.scheduler reduce_on_plateau → cosine,
  3. data.val_split 0.15→0.10 and data.test_split 0.10→0.0, growing the train pool 293 → 371 frames (+27%).

Two configs isolate it — configs/multiclass_experiment_256_base_cos.yaml (no augmentation beyond the settled noise_std=0.02) and configs/multiclass_experiment_256_scale_cos.yaml (scale_prob=0.5 only). Both match bf64_allaug on every other training-relevant field, and both logged train: 371 val: 54 — the identical split.

Run (identical config except augmentation) high_cell9 DSC / prec low_cell6 DSC / prec Evaluated DSC / prec / rec bf64_base_cos — no augmentation 0.601 / 0.501 0.611 / 0.862 0.605 / 0.617 / 0.594 bf64_scale_cos — scale augmentation 0.594 / 0.503 0.754 / 0.857 0.671 / 0.649 / 0.695 bf64_allaug — combined augmentation 0.482 / 0.365 0.693 / 0.837 0.572 / 0.515 / 0.643 (multiclass_experiment_256 — original, old schedule + split) 0.428 / 0.318 0.649 / 0.708 0.525 / 0.454 / 0.622

What this establishes, and what it retracts:

  1. The combined recipe's gain was schedule + data, not augmentation. No augmentation at all under the same setup scores 0.605, above bf64_allaug's 0.572.
  2. bf64_scale_cos is the new best real-holdout checkpoint at 0.671 (+0.066 over the matched baseline). Scale augmentation is the one augmentation lever that genuinely works.
  3. Combined augmentation is worse than doing nothing under a matched config (0.572 vs 0.605), so cutout_prob and/or brightness_contrast_prob are actively costing performance — which of the two is unknown.
  4. "Two cells, two opposite failure modes" is retracted as a magnitude claim. Matched, the two cells sit at 0.601 and 0.611 — a 0.010 gap, not 0.22. Likewise "scale augmentation hurts high_cell9": matched, it costs 0.007, inside run-to-run noise, not 0.060. high_cell9's over-segmentation at high laser power is still real and still undiagnosed; it is simply not a differently-sized problem.

The methodological lesson — don't repeat it

Every retracted finding here came from the same mistake: comparing runs that differed in more than one setting. The per-cell reporting discipline adopted on 2026-09-04 was correct and did catch a real regression — but it was applied to a comparison whose baseline had silently drifted, so it validated a confounded result for six days. When a run changes a non-augmentation setting (schedule, split, width, seed), it is not comparable to runs that didn't — re-run the baseline under the new setting before reporting a delta. Convenience changes like reclaiming an unused split are exactly the ones that slip through, because they don't feel like experimental variables.

Also confirmed: the internal validation split carried no signal on this comparison at all. bf64_base_cos scored 0.9285 internally and bf64_scale_cos 0.9277 — a 0.001 spread — while the development set separated the same two checkpoints by 0.066.

Both charts in the progress reports are generated from results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl by scripts/report/plot_percell_metrics.py and scripts/report/plot_sweep_dsc.py, so no figure can drift from the run that produced it.

docs.title: Loss function
docs.text:
The combined Dice + BCE loss used in binary-mode runs (Run 1–2, and binary_experiment_*.yaml):

Loss = α × BCE(pos_weight) + (1 − α) × Dice
  • BCE penalises each pixel individually — gives stable gradients early in training.
  • Dice measures overall mask overlap — keeps the model focused on the cell region rather than pixel counts.
  • pos_weight multiplies the BCE penalty on cell pixels to counter the 550:1 background/cell imbalance.

Current defaults in configs/default.yaml:

training:
  loss_alpha: 0.3        # Dice carries 70% of the loss signal
  loss_pos_weight: 100.0 # increase if recall is low; decrease if precision is low

Multiclass mode (unet.out_channels > 1, e.g. multiclass_experiment_256.yaml) replaces BCE with Cross-Entropy and Dice is computed per-class then averaged:

Loss = α × CrossEntropy(class_weights) + (1 − α) × mean(Dice per class)

class_weights (e.g. [1.0, 3.0, 3.0] for background/trapped_cell/other-decoy) plays the same role as pos_weight but is not directly comparable in magnitude — CrossEntropyLoss's weighted-mean reduction renormalises by weight mass, so porting pos_weight=100 in directly collapsed precision to ~0.13 by pushing recall to 1.0 everywhere. [1, 3, 3] was the winner of a small sweep (1,1,1 / 3,3,3 / 5,5,5 / 10,10,10 / 20,20,20, each trained the full 100 epochs) — trapped_cell precision=0.757/recall=0.813, a balanced result rather than recall-saturated.

docs.title: Expected trajectory (historical — see the 2026-09 sweep for the real number)
docs.text:
The table below was the pre-Run-4 projection and undershot: 220 masks reached DSC 0.943 on the (legacy-dominated) validation split, not the ~0.80-0.85 range extrapolated here. Kept for the historical record only — every number in this table is an internal-validation figure, and the full sweep above is the reason none of them should be trusted as a real-world estimate without a development-set or blind-test check behind them.

Masks Expected DSC (binary) Suggested pos_weight 30 ~0.72 100 40 0.76 (binary) / 0.78 (multiclass) — see Run 3 50 ~80 ~0.80 50–75 220 (historical) 0.943 internal-val / 0.538 on 5 real cells — see Domain Gap n/a (multiclass, class_weights=[1,3,3]) 425, full development-set eval (current) 0.605 (no augmentation) → 0.671 (scale augmentation) under the matched config — see the controlled re-run n/a

The thesis-reportable DSC comes from scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py on the 02_unet_holdout pool, which is now fully annotated and has been evaluated against every checkpoint in the sweep above. See Workflow Guide.

docs.title: Data Augmentation and Class-Imbalance Handling
docs.text:
Implemented, enabled on the train split only:

  • Horizontal flip (50% chance)
  • Vertical flip (50% chance)
  • Random 90° rotation (0°, 90°, 180°, or 270°)

CellDataset in scripts/training/train_unet.py applies these via augment=True (train split only — there's no separate test loader; see Data Layout).

Four more augmentation knobs were added during the 2026-09 sweep, all configured under training.augmentation and all off by default:

Knob What it does Result — see the sweep above noise_std Additive Gaussian noise on the frame Kept — confirmed net-positive alongside class_weights cutout_prob Erases one random rectangular patch (mean-filled), frame only Mixed in isolation with dropout; net-positive combined with everything else brightness_contrast_prob Random global brightness/contrast jitter No measurable effect alone scale_prob Random 0.7-1.3× resize of frame+mask together, then crop/pad back Helped one development cell, hurt the other, in isolation; net-positive combined

Originally, intensity augmentation (brightness/contrast) was excluded entirely on the reasoning that CLAHE in Stage 2 already normalises contrast, so jitter would just undo that work. Revisited once the sweep showed CLAHE normalises local contrast per-image, not the global exposure level a frame was captured at — added, tested, and found to have no measurable effect on its own (see above), though it's kept on in the current best combined recipe alongside three levers that do matter.

Note this augmentation section only addresses spatial/intensity invariance within a cell's own appearance — not the legacy/real-domain imbalance (see Domain Gap for domain_oversample_weight, tried and found not to help) and not the cell-size mismatch that turned out to matter far more (see the sweep above).

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
1. Current priority — retrain on the completed 445-frame pool. low_cell5 was annotated on 2026-09-10, taking 01_annotate_pool to 445/445 and adding a twelfth training cell. More real cell identities is historically the only lever to produce a large real-generalization improvement (the 2026-08-27 domain-gap closure), and it has never been combined with the current best recipe. Re-run scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks first — the preprocessed set is still at 425 — then train configs/multiclass_experiment_256_scale_cos.yaml on 445 frames across 23 groups. high_cell10 stays deliberately unannotated (see Data Layout — Cell roles for the full protocol and why).
  2. Ablate cutout_prob and brightness_contrast_prob separately. Combined augmentation costs 0.033 evaluated DSC against no augmentation at all, while scale alone gains 0.066 — so one or both of those two knobs is actively harmful, but which is unknown. One run each settles it.
  3. Investigate high_cell9's over-segmentation directly — overlay the predicted region on the raw, non-CLAHE frame across a few laser-power steps and check whether it visibly tracks a halo/glare shape. This is the one concrete diagnostic step from the augmentation experiments that hasn't been done yet, and the most direct route to closing high_cell9's remaining gap.
  4. Once the recipe is genuinely settled (no more hyperparameter changes queued): fold high_cell9 + low_cell6 into the training pool, train the final/production checkpoint once on the enlarged pool, then annotate high_cell10 and evaluate it exactly once — the blind test. See Data Layout for the exact sequence; do not annotate or evaluate high_cell10 before this is triggered.
  5. Train with full determinism (cudnn_deterministic=True, cudnn_benchmark=False, strict_deterministic=True) once more compute is available, and re-run the legacy-vs-domain-adapt breakdown from Domain Gap against whatever checkpoint is current at that point — the 0.910/0.939 figure has been unreproducible since 2026-08-29 and is still purely historical.
  6. Run the frozen U-Net (binary_output=True) over 03_mask_factory (608 frames) → extract features → train SVM / RF / DT classifiers.
  7. Biomechanics: compute RoD, correlate with laser power, fit Kelvin–Voigt model.

docs.title: Experiment rules (from 2026-09-17)
docs.text:
These came out of measuring run-to-run variance for the first time. They are not style preferences; two results have already been retracted for breaking them.

  1. One seed (42) while iterating, split_seed pinned at 42 too. Three seeds on both arms before anything is reported as a result.
  2. A single-seed delta below ~0.16 is not a result. Log it as screened, inconclusive. scripts/evaluation/compare_postswap.py prints this verdict for you.
  3. Change one variable per run. If a non-experimental setting moves — schedule, split, width, pool — re-run the baseline under it before quoting any delta.
  4. Check the split log line at the top of every run. high_cell10 is 50 frames against a ~45-frame validation target and lands in validation on 13% of seeds; when it does, that run trained without its only small cell and is void.
  5. Prefer levers big enough to see. The two effects that cleared the noise were a data change (+0.245 on high-9 after the cell exchange) and a resolution change (+0.048 for 128→256). No hyperparameter has come close.

End-to-end steps from raw video to trained models and evaluation results.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Stage 0          Stage 1        Annotation     Stage 2           Stage 3          Evaluation
─────────────    ────────────   ────────────   ───────────────   ──────────────   ──────────────
Organise    →   Extract    →   Annotate   →   Preprocess    →   Train U-Net  →   Evaluate
raw videos       frames         masks          (manual)          + Classify        holdout set

docs.title: Step 0 — Organise raw data
docs.text:
Build the three pipeline-ready frame folders from data/raw/. (There used to be a fourth, 04_clf_arena — collapsed into 03_mask_factory on 2026-09-03; see Data Layout if you run across a reference to it elsewhere.)

celldform-organize-dataset

Outputs — see Data Layout for the full breakdown, including the development-set/blind-test split inside 02_unet_holdout:

Folder Images Purpose data/frames/01_annotate_pool/ 445 U-Net training source — fully annotated as of 2026-09-10 (445/445; low_cell5 was the last outstanding cell) data/frames/02_unet_holdout/ 101 Development set (high_cell9 + low_cell6) — evaluated repeatedly to guide tuning, fully annotated data/frames/02_unet_holdout/final_test/ 50 Blind test (high_cell10) — reserved, deliberately unannotated, see Data Layout — Cell roles data/frames/03_mask_factory/ 608 U-Net inference → classifier training (12 cells; high_cell10 removed 2026-09-10 — it is the blind test and must not reach classifier training)

The current data on disk doesn't exactly match what a fresh celldform-organize-dataset run produces

The 2026-09-04 cell reallocation (high_cell10 → blind test, low_cell5 stays training) was done by moving files by hand, not by rerunning the organiser — see Data Layout before running --no-clean against the current pool.

docs.title: Step 1 — Annotate training images
docs.text:
Open each image in napari, paint the cell body on the mask layer, and press S to save.

python scripts/annotation/annotate.py
python scripts/annotation/annotate.py --multiclass   # experimental 3-class labels (see docs/scripts.md)

Keybindings:

Key Action 2 Paint brush 3 Eraser [ / ] Smaller / larger brush Ctrl+Z Undo S Save mask and advance N Skip (no save) B Previous image P Toggle paint mode (napari default)

The viewer loads every image in the pool, in order — including already-annotated ones, so you can browse back with B to review or fix earlier masks — but opens on the first not-yet-annotated image, so it's still safe to stop and resume at any time.

Toggle the enhanced layer in the napari layer list to see the CLAHE-boosted view for easier boundary identification.

docs.title: Step 2 — Validate masks
docs.text:
Confirm every image has a clean binary mask before preprocessing.

python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py
python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py --multiclass   # validates 0/1/2 label masks instead

Validates the masks that are present — does not require every frame to have a mask. Checks performed per mask found:

  • Readable — valid image file
  • Binary — pixel values are strictly 0 or 255 (--multiclass: 0, 1, or 2)
  • Non-empty — at least one cell pixel (255) present (--multiclass: at least one trapped-cell pixel, label 1)

Exits with code 0 if all present masks pass, 1 if any issues found. Safe to run incrementally while annotation is still in progress.

docs.title: Step 3 — Preprocess training data
docs.text:
Resize frames to 256×256 and resize masks to match. This must be run before training.

python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks

Only frames that have a corresponding mask are processed — frames without a mask are skipped automatically. This means you can run this step incrementally as you annotate more images; re-run it after each annotation session to keep the preprocessed data in sync.

Outputs:

data/preprocessed/train/01_annotate_pool/
  inputs/    ← 256×256 preprocessed frames  (U-Net training inputs)
  labels/    ← 256×256 binary masks         (U-Net training labels)

Optional — generate pipeline stage figures for thesis reporting:

python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks --compare --n-compare 10

docs.title: Step 4 — Train U-Net
docs.text:
python scripts/training/train_unet.py --config configs/default.yaml
# or
celldform-train-unet --config configs/default.yaml

Training reads from data/preprocessed/train/01_annotate_pool/. The dataset is automatically split into train / val (85 % / 15 % by default, data.val_split in the config) — val is a monitoring split only (checkpoint selection, early stopping), not the thesis-reportable score. That comes from scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py against the external 02_unet_holdout pool, which is why there's no third "test" split here — it would be redundant with that external evaluation (removed 2026-09-04).

Checkpoints are saved to checkpoints/:

File Contents unet_best.pt Best checkpoint by validation DSC unet_last.pt Final epoch checkpoint config.yaml Config snapshot for reproducibility

Which config to use

configs/multiclass_experiment_256.yaml is the frozen label scheme/resolution (decided 2026-08-10) and the config actually being trained on — its checkpoint lives at checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256/unet_best.pt, not checkpoints/unet_best.pt (that path is configs/default.yaml's binary/256×256 checkpoint, kept as a baseline but not the primary one). configs/binary_experiment_{128,256}.yaml and configs/multiclass_experiment.yaml (128×128) are the historical ablation that made that decision — see Training Results for the comparison and the domain-gap finding since. configs/multiclass_experiment_256_domain_oversample.yaml is an A/B variant (training.domain_oversample_weight: 8.0, own checkpoint dir) — tested, did not help, kept for the record.

docs.title: Step 5 — Evaluate on the development set
docs.text:
02_unet_holdout's top level (high_cell9 + low_cell6) is fully annotated as of 2026-09-03 and safe to evaluate against freely — see Data Layout for why this is called the development set, not a test set: every score from it is expected to shape a tuning decision, unlike the reserved blind test.

# 5a — validate development-set masks (already annotated — this just confirms nothing's broken)
python scripts/annotation/validate_masks.py --pool 02_unet_holdout --multiclass

# 5b — preprocess development-set data
python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --masks --pool 02_unet_holdout \
    --mask-dir data/masks/02_unet_holdout_multiclass \
    --output-dir data/preprocessed/evaluate/02_unet_holdout/inputs \
    --mask-output-dir data/preprocessed/evaluate/02_unet_holdout/labels

# 5c — evaluate: all cells, and per-cell (always check both — see the warning below)
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py --checkpoint checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt \
    --config checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/config.yaml
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py --checkpoint checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt \
    --config checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/config.yaml --filter high_cell9
python scripts/evaluation/evaluate_unet.py --checkpoint checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt \
    --config checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/config.yaml --filter low_cell6

Every run appends its full-precision metrics to results/preswap/preswap_eval_log.jsonl (--no-save-results to skip, --results-log to redirect) — that file, not a number copied into a doc or terminal scrollback, is the durable record.

Always check the per-cell breakdown, never trust the evaluated number alone

With only two development cells, the evaluated score is a frame-weighted blend, not an average, and it has hidden a real regression before: bf64_scale looked like a win over all cells (0.525→0.541) but actually made high_cell9 worse (0.428→0.368) while making low_cell6 much better — the --filter flags above exist specifically so this doesn't get missed again. See Training Results for the full story.

This is not the thesis-reportable blind-test number

The development set is evaluated repeatedly to guide tuning — that's the opposite of what a blind test needs. The one honest, one-shot generalization number comes from 02_unet_holdout/final_test/ (high_cell10), reserved and deliberately unannotated until the recipe is settled — see Data Layout — Cell roles for the full protocol.

Optional — legacy-domain diagnostic

data/frames/02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout/ holds 20 legacy frames reserved separately for a second, independent DSC — it isolates "the segmentation is weak" from "there's a domain gap between legacy microscope images and the real optical-tweezer setup." Repeat 5a–5c with --image-dir data/frames/02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout --mask-dir data/masks/02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout and separate --output-dir/--mask-output-dir for preprocessing. Report it as its own number — do not merge it with the DSC above.

docs.title: Step 6 — Run U-Net inference on mask factory
docs.text:
Not yet started as of 2026-09-04 — the U-Net recipe is still being tuned (see Training Results — Next Steps). This step generates predicted masks for the classifier training pool once it is.

celldform-harvest-factory            # ensemble s42-s45 -> data/factory/ensemble4, features -> results/factory

celldform-harvest-factory (scripts/inference/harvest_factory.py) segments every 03_mask_factory frame with the seed ensemble at native resolution and extracts the classifier features; see its docstring and --help. It replaced the command previously shown here (celldform-infer <image folder> ...), which never ran inference: the old celldform-infer was a stub that loaded the checkpoint and stopped.

checkpoints/unet_best.pt is not the right path

That default path belongs to configs/default.yaml (binary, 256×256) — not the frozen multiclass pipeline actually being trained. Use whatever checkpoint Training Results currently names as best (checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt as of 2026-09-10), and update this doc when that changes.

high_cell10 is not in this pool

It was removed on 2026-09-10 — as the U-Net's blind test it must not also feed classifier training. The pool is 608 frames across 12 cells.

docs.title: Step 7 — Train classifier
docs.text:
Feature extraction and classifier training (SVM / RF / DT) using the predicted masks from Step 6.

python scripts/inference/infer.py \
    --unet-ckpt checkpoints/multiclass_experiment_256_bf64_scale_cos/unet_best.pt \
    --classifier-ckpt checkpoints/svm.pkl

Cell-level cross-validation

Use leave-one-cell-out or group-k-fold with groups=cell_id. Never use frame-level CV — frames from the same cell are correlated.

docs.title: Step 8 — Final classifier evaluation
docs.text:
There is no separate classifier-only firewall pool anymore — 04_clf_arena was retired 2026-09-03 when its role merged into 02_unet_holdout (see Data Layout). The same three-tier discipline from Step 5 applies here too: use the development set (high_cell9/low_cell6) freely while building the classifier, and evaluate on the blind test (high_cell10) exactly once, at the same moment the U-Net's own blind test happens — not before.

python scripts/data/preprocess_frames.py --image-dir data/frames/02_unet_holdout/final_test \
    --output-dir data/preprocessed/inference/final_test/inputs

No command runs the full pipeline on a folder of frames yet

The celldform-infer <image folder> ... command previously shown here never worked (the old celldform-infer was a stub). Today celldform-infer takes a video (--video), and celldform-harvest-factory segments a pool and extracts features. The blind test needs a folder-based equivalent of one of them before it can run.

class FrameExtractor:
    """Extracts frames from a single optical tweezer video file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    video_path:
        Path to the source video (AVI, MP4, …).
    output_dir:
        Directory where extracted frames will be saved. *None* for stream-only use
        (:meth:`stream`), which writes nothing; the saving methods then raise.
    target_size:
        ``(width, height)`` to resize each frame.  Default ``(256, 256)``
        matches the U-Net input resolution.
    image_format:
        ``"png"`` (lossless) or ``"tiff"``.
    change_threshold:
        Minimum Euclidean displacement (pixels) of the trapped cell centroid
        between the current and the last saved frame required to save a new
        frame.  ``None`` disables tracking and saves every candidate frame.
    dark_percentile:
        Pixels at or below this intensity percentile *within the channel* are
        treated as cell candidates.  Default ``20`` (bottom 20 %).
    channel_width:
        Width of the vertical flow channel as a fraction of the image width,
        centred horizontally.  Default ``0.30`` (±15 % around the midpoint).
    min_circularity:
        Minimum circularity score (``4π·area/perimeter²``, 0–1) for a blob to
        be considered a cell.  Default ``0.60``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        video_path: str | os.PathLike,
        output_dir: Optional[str | os.PathLike] = "data/frames",
        target_size: Tuple[int, int] = (256, 256),
        image_format: str = "png",
        change_threshold: Optional[float] = None,
        dark_percentile: float = 20.0,
        channel_width: float = 0.30,
        min_circularity: float = 0.60,
    ) -> None:
        self.video_path = Path(video_path)
        self.output_dir = Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else None
        self.target_size = target_size
        self.image_format = image_format.lstrip(".")
        self.change_threshold = change_threshold
        self.dark_percentile = dark_percentile
        self.channel_width = channel_width
        self.min_circularity = min_circularity

        if self.output_dir is not None:
            self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def extract(
        self,
        every_n: Optional[int] = None,
        target_fps: Optional[float] = None,
        max_frames: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> List[np.ndarray]:
        """Extract frames to ``output_dir``.

        Temporal sampling (``every_n`` / ``target_fps``) is a coarse
        pre-filter.  When ``change_threshold`` is also set, each candidate is
        further tested — only frames where the trapped cell has moved are saved.

        Parameters
        ----------
        every_n:
            Keep every n-th frame.  Mutually exclusive with *target_fps*.
        target_fps:
            Resample to this frame rate.  Mutually exclusive with *every_n*.
        max_frames:
            Hard upper limit on saved frames.

        Returns
        -------
        List of saved frames as uint8 NumPy arrays (H × W).
        """
        if every_n is not None and target_fps is not None:
            raise ValueError("Specify either every_n or target_fps, not both.")

        frames: List[np.ndarray] = []
        manifest_rows: List[dict] = []

        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(self.video_path))
        if not cap.isOpened():
            raise IOError(f"Cannot open video: {self.video_path}")

        native_fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS) or 30.0
        step = self._compute_step(every_n, target_fps, native_fps)

        frame_idx = 0
        saved_idx = 0
        last_centroid: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None

        while True:
            ret, frame = cap.read()
            if not ret:
                break

            if frame_idx % step == 0:
                processed = self._process_frame(frame)
                centroid = _find_trapped_cell_centroid(
                    processed,
                    dark_percentile=self.dark_percentile,
                    channel_width=self.channel_width,
                    min_circularity=self.min_circularity,
                )
                displacement = _centroid_displacement(centroid, last_centroid)

                # Save if: first frame, tracking disabled, or cell has moved enough.
                if (
                    last_centroid is None
                    or self.change_threshold is None
                    or displacement > self.change_threshold
                ):
                    timestamp_s = frame_idx / native_fps
                    out_path = (
                        self.output_dir
                        / f"{self.video_path.stem}_{saved_idx:06d}.{self.image_format}"
                    )
                    cv2.imwrite(str(out_path), processed)
                    last_centroid = centroid

                    frames.append(processed)
                    manifest_rows.append({
                        "source": str(self.video_path),
                        "frame_index": frame_idx,
                        "saved_index": saved_idx,
                        "timestamp_s": round(timestamp_s, 6),
                        "centroid_x": round(centroid[0], 2) if centroid else None,
                        "centroid_y": round(centroid[1], 2) if centroid else None,
                        "displacement_px": round(displacement, 3) if displacement != float("inf") else None,
                        "output_path": str(out_path),
                        "width": processed.shape[1],
                        "height": processed.shape[0],
                    })
                    saved_idx += 1

                    if max_frames is not None and saved_idx >= max_frames:
                        break

            frame_idx += 1

        cap.release()
        self._write_manifest(manifest_rows)
        return frames

    def seek_extract(
        self,
        targets: List[int],
        file_stem: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> List[np.ndarray]:
        """Extract specific frames by index via direct seek.

        Unlike ``extract()``, this does not decode every intermediate frame —
        it calls ``cap.set(CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES)`` for each target, making it
        efficient for sparse sampling over large videos or network-mounted paths.

        Parameters
        ----------
        targets:
            Ordered list of frame indices to extract.
        file_stem:
            Base name for output files.  Defaults to ``video_path.stem``.
            Pass a clean string (e.g. ``"high_cell1"``) when the video filename
            contains spaces or other characters you don't want in filenames.

        Returns
        -------
        List of saved frames as uint8 NumPy arrays (H × W).
        """
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(self.video_path))
        if not cap.isOpened():
            raise IOError(f"Cannot open video: {self.video_path}")

        native_fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS) or 30.0
        stem = file_stem or self.video_path.stem

        frames: List[np.ndarray] = []
        manifest_rows: List[dict] = []

        for saved_idx, frame_index in enumerate(targets):
            cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, frame_index)
            ret, frame = cap.read()
            if not ret:
                continue

            processed = self._process_frame(frame)
            timestamp_s = frame_index / native_fps

            out_path = self.output_dir / f"{stem}_{frame_index:06d}.{self.image_format}"
            cv2.imwrite(str(out_path), processed)

            frames.append(processed)
            manifest_rows.append({
                "source":      str(self.video_path),
                "frame_index": frame_index,
                "saved_index": saved_idx,
                "timestamp_s": round(timestamp_s, 6),
                "output_path": str(out_path),
                "width":       processed.shape[1],
                "height":      processed.shape[0],
            })

        cap.release()
        self._write_manifest(manifest_rows)
        return frames

    def stream(
        self,
        every_n: int = 1,
    ) -> Generator[Tuple[int, float, np.ndarray], None, None]:
        """Yield ``(frame_index, timestamp_s, frame)`` without saving to disk.

        All candidate frames are yielded — change detection is not applied in
        stream mode so the downstream pipeline receives every frame.
        """
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(self.video_path))
        if not cap.isOpened():
            raise IOError(f"Cannot open video: {self.video_path}")

        native_fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS) or 30.0
        frame_idx = 0

        while True:
            ret, frame = cap.read()
            if not ret:
                break

            if frame_idx % every_n == 0:
                yield frame_idx, frame_idx / native_fps, self._process_frame(frame)

            frame_idx += 1

        cap.release()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Private helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _process_frame(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Convert to grayscale and resize to target_size."""
        gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        return cv2.resize(gray, self.target_size, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)

    @staticmethod
    def _compute_step(
        every_n: Optional[int],
        target_fps: Optional[float],
        native_fps: float,
    ) -> int:
        if every_n is not None:
            return max(1, int(every_n))
        if target_fps is not None:
            return max(1, int(round(native_fps / target_fps)))
        return 1

    def _write_manifest(self, rows: List[dict]) -> None:
        if not rows:
            return
        manifest_path = self.output_dir / f"00_{self.video_path.stem}_manifest.csv"
        with manifest_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
            writer.writeheader()
            writer.writerows(rows)

def organise(
    raw_dir: Path = DEFAULT_RAW_DIR,
    frames_dir: Path = DEFAULT_FRAMES_DIR,
    every_n: int = DEFAULT_EVERY_N,
    domain_adapt_n: int = DEFAULT_DA_N,
    clean: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Organise raw data into the three pipeline-ready frame folders."""
    t0     = time.time()
    videos = _video_lists(raw_dir)

    folders = {
        "annotate":  frames_dir / "01_annotate_pool",
        "unet_test": frames_dir / "02_unet_holdout",
        "inference": frames_dir / "03_mask_factory",
    }

    if clean and frames_dir.exists():
        print(f"Cleaning {frames_dir} ...", flush=True)
        shutil.rmtree(frames_dir)
    frames_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Legacy cancer images
    ann_dir   = folders["annotate"]
    ann_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    legacy_dir = raw_dir / "legacy/20210825_cancer"

    # A subset of legacy frames is permanently reserved as an untouched,
    # protocol-frozen holdout (data/frames/02_unet_holdout/legacy_holdout) —
    # used alongside 02_unet_holdout itself to separate "domain gap" from
    # "general holdout weakness" once the real U-Net holdout is evaluated.
    # Exclude those filenames here so re-running this step (e.g. --no-clean
    # after growing the domain-adapt pool) can never silently recopy them
    # back into the annotation pool.
    legacy_holdout_dir = folders["unet_test"] / "legacy_holdout"
    reserved_names = {p.name for p in legacy_holdout_dir.glob("*.jpg")} if legacy_holdout_dir.exists() else set()

    print("\n[annotate_pool] Copying legacy cancer images ...", flush=True)
    ann_rows: List[dict] = []
    for img in sorted(legacy_dir.glob("*.jpg")) + sorted(legacy_dir.glob("*.JPG")):
        if img.name in reserved_names:
            continue
        shutil.copy(img, ann_dir / img.name)
        ann_rows.append({
            "source":      str(img),
            "her2":        "unlabeled",
            "cell_id":     "legacy",
            "frame_index": "",
            "output_path": str(ann_dir / img.name),
        })
    print(f"  → {len(ann_rows)} images ({len(reserved_names)} legacy_holdout frames excluded)", flush=True)

    # Domain-adapt samples
    print("\n[annotate_pool] Adding 2025-camera domain samples ...", flush=True)
    da_rows = _domain_adapt(videos["domain_adapt"], ann_dir, domain_adapt_n, TARGET_SIZE)
    ann_rows.extend(da_rows)
    _write_csv(ann_dir / "00_manifest.csv", ann_rows)  # 00_ prefix sorts it above the frames
    print(f"  → {len(da_rows)} domain frames  ({len(ann_rows)} total in pool)", flush=True)

    # U-Net test hold-out
    print(f"\n[unet_holdout] → {folders['unet_test'].name}", flush=True)
    rows = _extract_group(videos["unet_test"], folders["unet_test"], every_n, TARGET_SIZE)
    print(f"  → {len(rows)} frames total", flush=True)

    # Mask factory (absorbed 04_clf_arena's cells 2026-09-03 — see module docstring)
    print(f"\n[mask_factory] → {folders['inference'].name}", flush=True)
    rows = _extract_group(videos["inference"], folders["inference"], every_n, TARGET_SIZE)
    print(f"  → {len(rows)} frames total", flush=True)

    # Summary
    print(f"\n{'─'*60}", flush=True)
    print("Dataset layout:", flush=True)
    for folder in folders.values():
        imgs = list(folder.glob("*.jpg")) + list(folder.glob("*.JPG"))
        print(f"  {folder.name:<32} {len(imgs):>5} images", flush=True)
    print(f"\nDone in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", flush=True)

docs.title: DeformationAnalyzer
docs.text:
Quantitative biomechanical analysis of cell deformation time-series.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default condition

The optical parameters used in this experiment. Can be set later via :meth:set_condition.

required metric str

Which feature column to use as the primary deformation signal. Defaults to "aspect_ratio"; any column from MorphologyExtractor works.

'aspect_ratio' window_s Optional[float]

class DeformationAnalyzer:
    """Quantitative biomechanical analysis of cell deformation time-series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    condition:
        The optical parameters used in this experiment.  Can be set later
        via :meth:`set_condition`.
    metric:
        Which feature column to use as the primary deformation signal.
        Defaults to ``"aspect_ratio"``; any column from MorphologyExtractor works.
    window_s:
        Sliding-window width in seconds for local RoD estimation.
        Pass *None* to skip sliding-window computation.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        laser_power_mW: float = 0.0,
        trap_current_mA: float = 0.0,
        metric: str = "aspect_ratio",
        window_s: Optional[float] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.condition = ExperimentCondition(
            laser_power_mW=laser_power_mW,
            trap_current_mA=trap_current_mA,
        )
        self.metric = metric
        self.window_s = window_s

    def set_condition(self, laser_power_mW: float, trap_current_mA: float) -> None:
        self.condition.laser_power_mW = laser_power_mW
        self.condition.trap_current_mA = trap_current_mA

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def deformation_rate(
        self,
        metric_values: np.ndarray,
        timestamps: np.ndarray,
    ) -> float:
        """Estimate mean deformation rate as a linear slope over time.

        Parameters
        ----------
        metric_values:
            1-D array of deformation metric values (e.g. deformation index).
        timestamps:
            1-D array of corresponding timestamps in seconds.

        Returns
        -------
        Mean deformation rate in metric-units / second (slope of linear fit).
        """
        if len(metric_values) < 2:
            return float("nan")

        # Linear fit: metric ~ slope * t + intercept
        slope, _, _, _, _ = stats.linregress(timestamps, metric_values)
        return float(slope)

    def sliding_rate(
        self,
        metric_values: np.ndarray,
        timestamps: np.ndarray,
    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Compute local deformation rate over a sliding window.

        Returns
        -------
        (window_centres, local_rates) — both 1-D arrays of the same length.
        """
        if self.window_s is None:
            raise ValueError("Set window_s in the constructor to use sliding_rate.")

        rates, centres = [], []
        dt = np.median(np.diff(timestamps))        # average sampling interval
        half = self.window_s / 2.0

        for t_c in timestamps:
            mask = (timestamps >= t_c - half) & (timestamps <= t_c + half)
            if mask.sum() < 2:
                continue
            slope, *_ = stats.linregress(timestamps[mask], metric_values[mask])
            rates.append(slope)
            centres.append(t_c)

        return np.array(centres), np.array(rates)

    def analyze_batch(
        self,
        experiments: List[Dict],
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Aggregate results across multiple experimental conditions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        experiments:
            List of dicts, each with keys:
            ``laser_power_mW``, ``trap_current_mA``,
            ``metric_values`` (array), ``timestamps`` (array).

        Returns
        -------
        DataFrame with columns: laser_power_mW, trap_current_mA,
        mean_rod, peak_deformation, n_frames.
        """
        rows = []
        for exp in experiments:
            mv = np.asarray(exp["metric_values"])
            ts = np.asarray(exp["timestamps"])
            rod = self.deformation_rate(mv, ts)
            rows.append(
                {
                    "laser_power_mW": exp["laser_power_mW"],
                    "trap_current_mA": exp["trap_current_mA"],
                    "mean_rod": rod,
                    "peak_deformation": float(np.nanmax(mv)),
                    "n_frames": len(mv),
                }
            )
        return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    def optical_correlation(
        self,
        summary_df: pd.DataFrame,
        x_col: str = "laser_power_mW",
        y_col: str = "mean_rod",
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Compute Pearson and Spearman correlation between an optical parameter
        and a deformation outcome across experimental conditions.

        Returns
        -------
        Dict with keys ``pearson_r``, ``pearson_p``, ``spearman_r``, ``spearman_p``.
        """
        x = summary_df[x_col].values
        y = summary_df[y_col].values

        pr, pp = stats.pearsonr(x, y)
        sr, sp = stats.spearmanr(x, y)

        return {
            "pearson_r": float(pr),
            "pearson_p": float(pp),
            "spearman_r": float(sr),
            "spearman_p": float(sp),
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Viscoelastic model fitting (Kelvin–Voigt)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def fit_kelvin_voigt(
        self,
        stress: np.ndarray,
        strain: np.ndarray,
        dt: float,
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Estimate E and η from the Kelvin–Voigt constitutive relation.

        σ(t) = E·ε(t) + η·dε/dt   (Eq. 2 in proposal)

        Uses finite differences for dε/dt and linear least-squares to solve
        for E and η simultaneously.

        Parameters
        ----------
        stress:
            Applied optical stress time-series.
        strain:
            Measured strain (deformation) time-series.
        dt:
            Sampling interval in seconds.

        Returns
        -------
        Dict with ``E`` (Young's modulus) and ``eta`` (viscosity coefficient).
        """
        d_strain = np.gradient(strain, dt)   # dε/dt via central differences

        # Stack [ε, dε/dt] as the design matrix, solve σ = A @ [E, η]^T.
        A = np.column_stack([strain, d_strain])
        params, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, stress, rcond=None)

        return {"E": float(params[0]), "eta": float(params[1])}

class CellClassifier:
    """SVM classifier (RBF kernel) for low / high HER2 expression.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scale_features:
        Z-score normalise features before fitting / predicting.
    random_state:
        Seed for reproducibility.
    **kwargs:
        Additional keyword arguments forwarded to :class:`sklearn.svm.SVC`.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        scale_features: bool = True,
        random_state: int = 42,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        self.scale_features = scale_features
        self.scaler = StandardScaler() if scale_features else None
        self._model = CalibratedClassifierCV(
            SVC(kernel="rbf", C=1.0, gamma="scale", random_state=random_state, **kwargs)
        )
        self._is_fitted = False

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def fit(
        self,
        X: "pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray",
        y: np.ndarray,
    ) -> "CellClassifier":
        """Train on feature matrix *X* and binary labels *y* (0 or 1)."""
        X_arr = self._to_array(X)
        if self.scaler is not None:
            X_arr = self.scaler.fit_transform(X_arr)
        self._model.fit(X_arr, y)
        self._is_fitted = True
        return self

    def predict(self, X: "pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray") -> np.ndarray:
        """Predict class labels (0 = low, 1 = high) for *X*."""
        self._check_fitted()
        return self._model.predict(self._transform(X))

    def predict_proba(self, X: "pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray") -> np.ndarray:
        """Return class probabilities, shape (n_samples, 2)."""
        self._check_fitted()
        return self._model.predict_proba(self._transform(X))

    def evaluate(
        self,
        X: "pd.DataFrame | np.ndarray",
        y: np.ndarray,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return accuracy, classification report, and AUC-ROC."""
        preds = self.predict(X)
        report = classification_report(y, preds, output_dict=True)
        proba = self.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]
        return {
            "accuracy": report["accuracy"],
            "classification_report": report,
            "auc_roc": roc_auc_score(y, proba),
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Serialisation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def save(self, path: "str | Path") -> None:
        """Persist the fitted classifier and scaler to *path*."""
        payload = {
            "model": self._model,
            "scaler": self.scaler,
            "is_fitted": self._is_fitted,
        }
        with open(Path(path), "wb") as fh:
            pickle.dump(payload, fh)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: "str | Path") -> "CellClassifier":
        """Restore a serialised classifier from *path*."""
        with open(Path(path), "rb") as fh:
            payload = pickle.load(fh)
        obj = cls.__new__(cls)
        obj._model = payload["model"]
        obj.scaler = payload["scaler"]
        obj.scale_features = obj.scaler is not None
        obj._is_fitted = payload["is_fitted"]
        return obj

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Private helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _transform(self, X: Any) -> np.ndarray:
        arr = self._to_array(X)
        if self.scaler is not None:
            arr = self.scaler.transform(arr)
        return arr

    @staticmethod
    def _to_array(X: Any) -> np.ndarray:
        if isinstance(X, pd.DataFrame):
            return X.values.astype(np.float32)
        return np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float32)

    def _check_fitted(self) -> None:
        if not self._is_fitted:
            raise RuntimeError("Call fit() before predict().")

        perimeter are converted to μm² and μm respectively.  Pass *None* to
        keep pixel units.
    min_area_px:
        Regions smaller than this (pixels) are discarded as noise.
    """

    _FEATURE_NAMES = [
        "area", "perimeter",
        "major_axis", "minor_axis",
        "aspect_ratio", "eccentricity",
        "circularity", "solidity",
        "hu_0", "hu_1", "hu_2", "hu_3", "hu_4", "hu_5", "hu_6",
    ]

    def __init__(
        self,
        pixel_size_um: Optional[float] = None,
        min_area_px: int = 50,
    ) -> None:
        self.pixel_size_um = pixel_size_um
        self.min_area_px = min_area_px

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public API
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def extract(self, mask: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Extract features from a single binary mask.

        Parameters
        ----------
        mask:
            uint8 array (H × W) with cell pixels = 1, background = 0.

        Returns
        -------
        Dict mapping feature name → float value.
        Returns a dict of NaN values if no valid region is found.
        """
        region = self._largest_region(mask)
        if region is None:
            return {k: float("nan") for k in self._FEATURE_NAMES}

        return self._compute_features(region)

    def batch(
        self,
        masks: List[np.ndarray],
        frame_ids: Optional[List[int]] = None,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Extract features from a list of masks and return a DataFrame.

        Parameters
        ----------
        masks:
            List of binary uint8 masks.
        frame_ids:
            Optional list of integer frame indices used as the DataFrame index.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas DataFrame with one row per mask and one column per feature.
        """
        rows = [self.extract(m) for m in masks]
        df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=self._FEATURE_NAMES)
        if frame_ids is not None:
            df.index = frame_ids
        return df

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Private helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _largest_region(self, mask: np.ndarray):
        """Return the skimage RegionProperties of the largest valid region."""
        labeled = measure.label(mask > 0)
        regions = measure.regionprops(labeled)

        # Filter tiny noise blobs.
        valid = [r for r in regions if r.area >= self.min_area_px]
        if not valid:
            return None

        # Select the region with the largest area (the target cell).
        return max(valid, key=lambda r: r.area)

    def _compute_features(self, region) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Derive all features from a skimage RegionProperties object."""
        area = float(region.area)
        perimeter = float(region.perimeter)

        # Axis lengths from the fitted ellipse.
        major = float(region.axis_major_length)
        minor = float(region.axis_minor_length) + 1e-8  # avoid division by zero

        aspect_ratio = major / minor
        eccentricity = float(region.eccentricity)
        circularity = 4 * np.pi * area / (perimeter ** 2 + 1e-8)
        solidity = float(region.solidity)

        # Hu moment invariants (7 values, log-scaled for numerical stability).
        mask_uint8 = (region.image.astype(np.uint8)) * 255
        moments = cv2.moments(mask_uint8)
        hu_raw = cv2.HuMoments(moments).flatten()
        hu = np.sign(hu_raw) * np.log10(np.abs(hu_raw) + 1e-30)

        # Optionally convert pixel units to physical units.
        if self.pixel_size_um is not None:
            area *= self.pixel_size_um ** 2
            perimeter *= self.pixel_size_um
            major *= self.pixel_size_um
            minor *= self.pixel_size_um

        return {
            "area": area,
            "perimeter": perimeter,
            "major_axis": major,
            "minor_axis": minor,
            "aspect_ratio": aspect_ratio,
            "eccentricity": eccentricity,
            "circularity": circularity,
            "solidity": solidity,
            **{f"hu_{i}": float(hu[i]) for i in range(7)},
        }

docs.title: feature_mask(model, processed, size=FEATURE_SIZE, crop_box=None)
docs.text:
Trapped-cell mask at size (width, height) for feature extraction.

Resamples the model's per-class probabilities (bilinear) and argmaxes at the target size, rather than upsampling the argmaxed 256 mask, which would leave a 4.8 x 3.6 px staircase on the boundary and bias perimeter and circularity. Works with :class:UNet and :class:~celldform.segmentation.ensemble.EnsembleUNet. Decoy pixels (class 2) are never foreground, the same contract as predict(binary_output=True).

crop_box (x0, y0, x1, y1), in full-frame pixels, is for models fed a crop of the frame (preprocessing crop_size): the prediction is resampled to the box and pasted back, and everything outside it is background.

Source code in celldform/integration/realtime.py 
def feature_mask(model: Any, processed: np.ndarray,
                 size: Tuple[int, int] = FEATURE_SIZE,
                 crop_box: Optional[Tuple[int, int, int, int]] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Trapped-cell mask at *size* ``(width, height)`` for feature extraction.

    Resamples the model's per-class **probabilities** (bilinear) and argmaxes at the
    target size, rather than upsampling the argmaxed 256 mask, which would leave a
    4.8 x 3.6 px staircase on the boundary and bias perimeter and circularity. Works
    with :class:`UNet` and :class:`~celldform.segmentation.ensemble.EnsembleUNet`.
    Decoy pixels (class 2) are never foreground, the same contract as
    ``predict(binary_output=True)``.

    ``crop_box`` (x0, y0, x1, y1), in full-frame pixels, is for models fed a crop of the
    frame (preprocessing ``crop_size``): the prediction is resampled to the box and pasted
    back, and everything outside it is background.
    """
    probs = model.predict_proba(processed)                          # (C, h, w)
    if crop_box is None:
        return _fg_from_probs(probs, size)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = crop_box
    full = np.zeros((size[1], size[0]), dtype=np.uint8)
    full[y0:y1, x0:x1] = _fg_from_probs(probs, (x1 - x0, y1 - y0))
    return full
